rulings.detail: Keep all 6 ORI9s; the block total of 689 is a correct sum, not double counting, and no canonical merge should be applied. The three zero members (CA0019916, CA0019947, CA0019991) are genuine 12-month NIBRS zeros — commercial-vehicle enforcement facilities and an investigative services unit have no Part-I patrol volume — keep as zeros, do not fill.
rulings.rationale: For CHP the last two ORI9 characters identify a physically separate Area Office or enforcement facility, not a lane variant: Oakland, Hayward and Dublin Area Offices patrol different Alameda County freeway segments and the FBI roster names all six independently. There is no …00 stem reporting in 2024, so there is no parent rollup the members could be duplicating, and none carries the covering-city name/footprint signature of a NIBRS-lane twin. The vectors are unrelated (MVT 385 / 168 / 16) and the trajectories move independently — Oakland rises 105→259→444 while Hayward goes 110→622→207 — which is inconsistent with the same incidents being counted twice. statewide_overlap_layer is an accumulation layer built for additive mass, so a shared footprint is not itself evidence of duplication.

rulings.detail: Keep all 14 ORI9s. Block total 486 for 2024 is correct as reported; no member collapses into CA0199935. Why the shared ORI7 is not evidence of double counting: CA01999xx is the FBI's state-agency ORI convention (CA019 = Los Angeles County, 99 = state agency operating in that county), so the shared ORI7 encodes 'state agency in LA County', not a parent/child rollup — and the packet confirms no ...00 stem (CA0199900) exists, so the ...00-stem twin rule has nothing to key on. Why the shared footprint is not evidence either: the crosswalk is marked 'overlap', not 'exclusive' — statewide_overlap_layer is the designed mechanism for agencies with no assignable exclusive territory, so co-residence there is intended, not duplication. SECONDARY: CA0199901 'Southern Division' reports 6, not the 486 group sum, so it is not a rollup parent. HYGIENE: five members (CA0199910, CA0199901, CA0199941, CA0199945, CA0199998) carry '(blank)' panel names while the roster has proper names, and their crosswalk rows are flagged_auto — a name-backfill gap worth fixing separately.
rulings.rationale: CHP is organized Division -> Area Office, and each Area Office is a distinct physical command with its own station, personnel and patrol territory; East LA, Newhall, Antelope Valley and West Valley are geographically separate parts of LA County covering different freeway corridors, and the FBI roster lists all 14 as separately named agencies. The 2024 offense vectors are operationally distinct rather than nested or duplicated — East LA is MVT-dominant (62 of 94), Santa Fe Springs is agg-assault-dominant (36 of 53), and the Southern Investigative Services Unit is larceny-only (35 of 36) — which is what separate units look like, not what one agency's duplicate feeds look like. The real overlap risk on this footprint is CHP-versus-local double counting (a freeway vehicle theft appearing in both CHP and LAPD/LASD counts), which is a jurisdictional-overlap problem and is exactly why these sit on a non-exclusive layer.

rulings.detail: Keep all 10 ORI9s. Block total 126 is correct and involves no double counting. The shared ORI7 CA03699 is CHP's Inland Division numbering block, not a single reporting entity; the ORI9 suffix identifies the area office. CA0369901 (Inland Division) and CA0369908 (Investigative Services Unit) are the only candidate rollup parents and both report 0 in 2024, confirming no parent aggregates the children.
rulings.rationale: CHP area offices are separate operational commands each patrolling a disjoint geographic beat — Victorville, Barstow, Rancho Cucamonga, Needles, San Bernardino — so their incident counts are additive, not overlapping; an incident on I-15 near Barstow is Barstow's and cannot also be Victorville's. The 2024 FBI roster names all ten distinctly, and their year-to-year trajectories move independently (Victorville 20/98/57/56 versus Barstow 8/11/29/39), which a single agency split across duplicate ORIs would not do. The shared 06:statewide_overlap_layer footprint is the crosswalk's coarse default for every state agency with no place assignment, not a claim of coincident jurisdiction — treating it as evidence of duplication would force a merge of every CHP office in California. The absence of a reporting CA0369900 stem removes the one structure that would signal a parent/child double count.

rulings.detail: Keep all three ORI9s. Correct 2024 block total is 108 (CA0429950=46, CA0429960=37, CA0429955=25). No canonical ORI, no merge, no supersession. The 62 counts riding above the largest member are real and must stay.

The shared 06:statewide_overlap_layer footprint is the deliberate catch-all for state and special-jurisdiction agencies that cannot be assigned to a place; it is marked 'overlap' rather than 'exclusive', and every CHP office in California lands there by design, so co-location on it is not evidence of duplicated incidents. Counts and vectors differ materially (larceny/MVT 5/41, 10/27, 7/18), and the identical nibrs_start of 2021-11-01 with matching 2-month 2021 stubs reflects one statewide CHP onboarding date, not one agency.

The counts diverge in every year on record (2021: 78 vs 56; 2022: 355 vs 167; 2023: 356 vs 194; 2024: 314 vs 140) and the 2024 offense vectors differ in both level and mix (larceny 65 / MVT 249 versus larceny 37 / MVT 103) — a double-submitted single agency produces identical or near-identical vectors, which is what the already-run identical-vector merge rule would have caught. There is also no …00 stem reporting in 2024, so no rollup parent exists that either member could be duplicating.

rulings.detail: Keep both. OK0550200 = Del City Police Department, 777, footprint 40:municipal:place:4019900 — correct as-is. OK055025C = Oklahoma Department of Corrections, 133, a state correctional agency. No merge, no supersession; the block total of 910 is not double counting and the 133 must NOT be collapsed onto Del City. Two follow-ups that are footprint problems, not dedup problems: (1) OK055025C carries name '(blank)' and type 'unknown' in the panel while the FBI 2024 roster names it — adopt the roster name and type so it stops presenting as a Del City twin; (2) its 15 murders and 37 rapes ride 40:statewide_overlap_layer at w=1, smearing institutional-population incidents across all of Oklahoma residential geography, which should be reviewed separately.

No municipality on earth produces that vector; it is a correctional system's PREA and inmate-death reporting. Every identifying field also diverges: roster names (Del City Police Department vs Oklahoma Department of Corrections), types (City vs Other State Agency), counties (OKLAHOMA vs NOT SPECIFIED), FBI population served (21,151 vs 0), and footprints (exclusive municipal place vs statewide overlap layer). This is not an ORI succession either — the active windows OVERLAP, both carrying positive counts across 2022-2024, so the shared ORI7 stem is an artifact of Oklahoma's ORI construction (county 055 = Oklahoma County) with a '5C' facility extension, not shared identity.

rulings.detail: One agency, two ORIs. Survivor / mass carrier: CT0050400 (the live submitter). CT0016900 must stop carrying mass from 2021 forward; its 2018-2020 rows are the same agency's earlier history and can be merged under the surviving record. CT0050400's identity metadata is defective (type 'unknown', county <NA>, place <NA>, agency_master_fallback footprint) and should be replaced with CT0016900's (special_jurisdiction, CT cty009, plc52000 New Haven). Correct footprint is a New Haven campus overlay, not statewide_overlap_layer — as it stands both ORIs smear 277 each over the whole state, double-counting 554. If downstream prefers a merge framing, the merged record is CT0050400's counts on CT0016900's identity.
rulings.rationale: The single deciding fact: from 2022 onward CT0016900 has NO FBI submission at all (SRS 0/0mo in 22, 23, 24) — its only rows are CIUS published rows, and CIUS derives FROM the FBI submission, so those rows ARE CT0050400's 12-month submission republished under the retired ORI, not independent data. That is why the vectors are byte-identical across three consecutive years including the distinctive 46/194/31 tail. The active windows are non-overlapping with a lane change at the break: CT0016900 submits SRS-only through 2020 (102/8mo) then dies, CT0050400 appears in 2020 (138/4mo, NIBRS+SRS) and runs 12mo from 2021 — 8+4 months partitioning the handover year, with 102+138=240 sitting exactly between the 2019 (261) and 2021 (173) campus levels. Both ORIs are absent from the 2024 CDE roster, so roster presence cannot arbitrate direction; submission liveness does.

rulings.detail: Canonical ORI9 = MA009639E. Supersede MA009IT00 so only ONE 295-count mass lands. Correct the canonical record's display name from 'CAMBRIDGE' — the covering-city name carried by the NIBRS batch header — to the roster name 'Massachusetts Institute of Technology'. Footprint: BOTH ORIs currently sit on 25:statewide_overlap_layer at w=1, which is wrong for either. MIT PD is a campus force inside Cambridge city, Middlesex County; the correct footprint is a non-exclusive campus OVERLAP anchored on place 2511000 (Cambridge city) at weight <1, layered under Cambridge PD's exclusive municipal footprint — never the statewide layer. Note MA009IT00 already carries plc11000 (Cambridge city) with a mislabeled census_name 'state of massachusetts'; that place code, not the statewide layer, is the right anchor to carry forward onto MA009639E.
rulings.rationale: The two ORIs carry byte-identical 7-offense vectors in seven consecutive years (2018-2024) in the same county FIPS 017, with a clean cross-lane split — MA009639E arriving via NIBRS, MA009IT00 via SRS — which is the documented duplication mechanism, not a coincidence pattern. The single deciding fact is the FBI 2024 roster: it lists MA009639E as 'Massachusetts Institute of Technology' (University or College, Middlesex) and does not list MA009IT00 at all, making the NIBRS ORI the live record and the legacy SRS stem dead. The name inversion is the expected NIBRS-twin artifact — the NIBRS variant displays the covering-city name while the legacy stem displays the correct agency name — so name quality must not be mistaken for ORI survivorship here.

rulings.detail: Canonical ORI = MI1176600 (Lincoln Township Police Department, Berrien County), footprint 26:municipal:cousub:2602147600 (Lincoln charter township) — already correct, keep as-is. MI0153300 must stop carrying mass entirely and should carry ZERO, not a fill: its CIUS rows are a name-collision mis-key of Lincoln Township's published data onto the Lincoln village (Alcona County) ORI, and it has no independent data of its own to preserve. Do not let the differing county FIPS (001 vs 021) or differing footprints block the merge — the geographic mismatch IS the defect. The 2022 discrepancy (CIUS 149 vs NIB/SRS 153) is an as-published-vs-revised difference, not evidence of a second agency. Recommend a parser guard: reject a CIUS row whose implied all-offence rate exceeds a hard ceiling (e.g. 10,000/100k) against the target ORI's own FBI population.
rulings.rationale: The single decisive fact is the rate: MI0153300's FBI population served is 301-315 people, and 146 Part-I offences over 301 residents is ~48,500/100k, roughly thirty times the national rate and physically impossible; the identical 146 over Lincoln Charter Township's 14,864 residents is ~982/100k, entirely normal. MI0153300 also records SRS 0 total at 0 MONTHS in every single year 2018-2024 and is ABSENT from the 2024 FBI roster, so it has never submitted anything — every value it carries arrives via the CIUS lane, which is where the mis-key happens. The byte-identical vectors in 2018 (189), 2019 (185), 2023 (165) and 2024 (146) match MI1176600's SRS values exactly, and a 301-person Michigan village almost certainly has no police department at all. Cross-lane split plus impossible rate plus zero own submissions leaves no coincidence reading.

rulings.detail: Canonical ORI = MN0030600 (the only one on the FBI 2024 roster, listed as "White Earth Tribal", Tribal, is_nibrs since 2017-02-01). MNDI01900 must stop carrying mass — it is the BIA-series shadow ORI for the same White Earth Tribal Police Department and is ABSENT from the 2024 roster. Footprint: BOTH current footprints are wrong and the merge must not inherit either. 27:statewide_overlap_layer smears a tribal PD's 171 offenses across 5.7M Minnesotans; 27:municipal:place:2770006 (White Earth CDP, ~600 people) would imply ~28,000/100k. Correct footprint is the White Earth Reservation AIANNH area spanning Becker (005), Mahnomen and Clearwater counties (~9-10k served, giving a plausible ~1,700/100k). If the crosswalk has no AIANNH layer, escalate the footprint separately rather than defaulting to statewide.

The 2018/2019 near-misses (307/278, 204/203) are lane-revision noise, not two agencies. The single fact that decided it: both ORIs sit in the same county with the same name and the same year-by-year vectors, split cleanly across the two FBI submission lanes — the documented duplication mechanism. Roster presence decides which survives; the footprint is a separate defect that the merge must not silently propagate.

rulings.detail: Canonical ORI9: NC092109E (the ORI the FBI's own 2024 CDE roster identifies as 'WakeMed Campus Police', Other, Wake County). NC092109E displays the known NIBRS-lane artifact exactly: it carries the covering-city batch-header name 'RALEIGH' while the ...00 stem carries the true agency name and crosswalk. The vectors are byte-identical across five consecutive years (2020-2024, 2024 = 0/0/1/7/10/83/2), the county FIPS match (183/Wake), the footprints match, and the lanes are split (NIBRS vs SRS) — the textbook duplication mechanism.

rulings.detail: Canonical ORI9 = NY054119E (Cornell University Police). Retire NY254UC00: drop its 2024 mass entirely and re-key its pre-2020 rows (2018 CIUS/SRS 229, 2019 SRS 158/9mo) onto NY054119E so the agency keeps its history. Correct footprint: neither ORI's current 36:statewide_overlap_layer is right for a campus PD — the merged agency should carry a Tompkins County campus overlay (Ithaca city / town of Ithaca, non-exclusive, overlap weight) so it neither smears across New York State nor subtracts from Ithaca PD's place mass.
rulings.rationale: Byte-identical 7-offence vectors in 2020 (149), 2023 (252) and 2024 (0/5/0/0/8/266/1 = 280), same county FIPS 109, same footprint, with the split running exactly along the known cross-lane duplication mechanism (NY054119E on NIBRS, NY254UC00 on CIUS/SRS) — and the NIBRS-lane ORI carries the covering-city name 'ITHACA' per the known twin artifact while the FBI's own 2024 roster resolves it to 'Cornell University', Tompkins. The single deciding fact for canonicity: NY054119E is on the FBI CDE 2024 roster and NY254UC00 is ABSENT, so the live ORI must carry the mass. Active windows overlap 2019-2024, so this is a live duplicate, not an ORI succession — both masses are currently landing on one geography.

rulings.detail: The printed 0 means 'did not report'. Set AL0080200 2024 to missing and fill. Own-history fill is permitted and well-anchored: 2022 and 2023 are both full 12-month NIBRS years, CIUS-corroborated, at 32 and 31, both within the 2-year window — fill at ~31.5 with the 2023 offense split. Do not treat the NIBRS 12-month batch header as decisive for this ORI: its own record shows the NIBRS lane printing 0 while real crime occurred (2019 NIB 0/1mo against a true 20; 2020 NIB 0/1mo against a true 12), so a NIBRS zero here has demonstrated precedent as a false zero.
rulings.rationale: The single decisive fact is the prior-year baseline: 32 in 2022 and 31 in 2023, both full 12-month years, make P(observing exactly 0 | rate ~31/yr) = e^-31 = 3e-14 — statistically impossible as a genuine outcome. The history is flat, not decaying (30, 20, 12, 20, 32, 31), so this is a cliff rather than the endpoint of a trajectory, which is precisely what separates it from the Pequot Lakes zero in the same batch where the 2023 baseline was 2. If the fill looks wrong on inspection, check whether Blountsville PD disbanded and Blount County SO absorbed the footprint — but even under that branch the correct handling is supersession, not keeping 0 as a measurement.

rulings.detail: Do not certify the zero and do not fill from it. Hold as low-confidence pending Slocomb's 2024 NIBRS monthly detail: if the twelve submitted months carry zero Group A incidents of ANY type (including non-Part-I drug, vandalism, simple assault), the feed is dead and the year should become missing and fillable from the 2021-2022 level (~11-15); if non-Part-I Group A incidents are present, the Part-I zero is real and stands. Mass at stake is only ~11-15 offences on a 2,149 footprint, so this is a provenance question rather than a national-total risk.
rulings.rationale: The batch-header evidence and the base rate point in opposite directions and the packet cannot separate them. Unlike Hurley and Junction City, Slocomb has no prior full-period zero — its 2019 and 2023 zeros are 3-month and 2-month windows — while its last two genuine full years are 15 (2021) and 11 (2022), so a true zero requires the underlying rate to have collapsed rather than continued down. Coverage also broke and returned (12mo 2022 → 2mo 2023 → 12mo 2024), and a returning filer posting twelve empty months is equally consistent with an export that resumed sending headers without incidents. Nothing here distinguishes an affirmative twelve-month zero-report from a revived-but-empty feed.

rulings.detail: The zero is unusable; mark 2024 missing and fillable. Fill from own history, annualizing the partial years first: 2023 = 6 at 6mo -> 12, 2022 = 15 at 10mo -> 18, 2021 = 15 at 11mo -> 16; scaling for the 20% population loss (3,265 -> 2,610) gives ~12-14. Recommend ~13. SECOND READING that downstream must resolve: Marion PD may have ceased operating and been absorbed by the Perry County SO — if so the fix is a footprint reassignment, not a fill, because the SO sits on state_nonmunicipal_remainder and would exclude Marion city entirely. Either reading forbids publishing a hard zero on this w=1 exclusive municipal footprint.
rulings.rationale: Same lane-month contradiction as the other 2024 zeros: NIB claims 12 months while SRS records ZERO months, the twelve-zero-report-headers signature rather than a measurement. The trajectory is decisive against a real zero — months coverage fell 11, 10, 6 across 2021-2023 while counts ran 15/15/6, and then 2024 claims coverage JUMPED from 6 months to 12 while output fell to zero; an agency that doubles its month coverage does not stop recording crime. Against a declining lambda of roughly 6-15, a genuine full-year zero runs between e^-6 (0.25%) and e^-15. I hold this at medium rather than high because Marion's lambda is small and its history is chaotic (2019 was a legitimate 5 at 12 months), and because the defunct-department alternative changes the correct repair even though it does not change the verdict.

rulings.detail: Treat 2024 as missing and fillable. Do not carry the printed 0. Fill from own CIUS history anchored on the two most recent real full years (2022=8, 2023=5), i.e. roughly 5-6, NOT the 6-year median 9.5 which is dragged up by 2018-2019 (17, 11) and ignores the monotone decline. Peer-rate fill is structurally unavailable: FBIpop is 0/null for every year of this ORI. Separately flag that this ORI sits on 06:statewide_overlap_layer w=1, so whatever value lands gets smeared across all of California — a campus agency's counts should not ride a statewide layer.
rulings.rationale: Textbook BLANK-AS-ZERO: the SRS Return-A lane records months_reported=0 for 2024 and there is no NIBRS row at all, so the agency submitted nothing to the FBI for that year, yet the CIUS table prints 0 in all seven cells. CIUS is derived from the FBI submission and is never independent corroboration of it, so the 12mo/tier-high/weight-1.0 label is entirely the pipeline's default assumption, not a measurement. The agency reported real positive values as recently as 2023 (CIUS 5, on a 4-month SRS submission), so it was not dormant. A zero-month submission cannot be rescued by uplift and cannot stand as a measured zero.

rulings.detail: Drop the 2024 zero; mark CA0470700 2024 missing and fillable. Own-history fill is licensed (real report 2023, within 2 years): CIUS-lane median 6 across 2018/2019/2022/2023, so fill ~6 Part-I. Also correct the 2021 panel value — SRS 0 at 0 months is a non-report being carried as a literal zero, which is depressing this agency's own baseline.
rulings.rationale: This ORI has a documented history of the exact failure mode in question: in 2022 the NIBRS lane reported 0 across a 7-month header while the CIUS-published value for the same agency-year was 4. That is direct, agency-specific proof that a NIBRS zero from Tulelake does not mean zero crime, which disposes of the 'decisive provenance' framing of the 12-month 2024 header. Against that, 2024 shows the full BLANK-AS-ZERO signature — printed full-year zero, SRS submission record of 1 month, and CIUS/NIB/SRS carrying one identical vector rather than three independent confirmations. A stable positive history (6, 7, 11, 4, 6) in an 856-person town makes a categorical seven-class zero a sub-1% event on its own terms.

rulings.detail: The printed 0 is not a measurement. Set GA0710300 2024 to missing. Fill is less clean than Blountsville because the immediately preceding year is itself a non-report (2023 SRS 0/0mo) and 2022 is only a 3-4 month partial (5 offenses): annualize 2022 first (5 x 12/3.5 = ~17-20) and cross-check against the last real full year 2021 (24), giving a defensible fill of ~20, or use GA small-town local_police peers. PRECONDITION on the fill: check whether Buchanan PD went dark and Haralson County SO absorbed the footprint — if so the correct handling is supersession under the existing dead-ORI rule rather than a fill. Either way 0 must not survive as an observed value.
rulings.rationale: The decisive fact is that the 2024 'complete 12-month zero report' emerges from a reporting vacuum: 2021 was the last full year (24), 2022 collapsed to a 3-4 month partial (5), and 2023 was a total non-report — a feed that decayed to nothing does not spontaneously produce a clean full-year submission, and P(0 | rate ~24/yr) = 4e-11 rules out a genuine zero. This ORI's NIBRS lane is demonstrably intermittent (NIB 4mo in 2019, 12mo in 2020-21, 4mo in 2022, none in 2023, then 12mo in 2024), so the 12-month batch header is far more likely a vendor or state auto-generated zero-month series than a real submission improvement. Contrast Pequot Lakes in this same batch, where a 12-month NIBRS zero follows an unbroken submission record and a prior-year baseline of 2 — Buchanan has neither.

rulings.detail: Accept 0 for 2024, but attach a watch flag rather than treating it as a settled structural fact: if 2025 also prints all-seven zeros, reclassify the 2022-2025 run as a decayed feed and refill from the pre-transition baseline (2018 20, 2019 28). Do not let this zero anchor any own-history fill for neighbouring agency-years.
rulings.rationale: The immediately preceding credible level makes a zero draw ordinary rather than extraordinary: 2023 was 2 at a 12-month NIBRS header (SRS 2 at 5mo annualizes to ~5), so P(0) is 3-14% — unremarkable for a 1,383-person village. The 12-month NIBRS batch header is an affirmative submission and the agency has filed 12-month NIBRS in 2022, 2023 and 2024. I explicitly do not treat the 28->7->6->2->0 slope as support (partial feeds decay smoothly); the ruling rests on the magnitude of the last measured level, and the pre-NIBRS baseline of 20-28 is the reason this is medium and not high.

rulings.detail: Treat the 2024 zero as a non-report; the agency-year should be missing and fillable. Fill from own history — the last real report is 2023 (=9), inside the 2-year recency rule; median of the non-zero best-values 2018-2023 (9, 8, 6, 5, 9) is 8. Footprint is a statewide overlap layer at w=1, so the mass impact is immaterial either way; the point is not to let a printed zero stand as a measurement.
rulings.rationale: The single decisive fact is that this ORI's own publication lane has a demonstrated false zero: in 2020 CIUS printed 0 (NoF7, 6 rows) while SRS carried 6 offenses in 3 months for the same agency-year. Against a stable campus history of 9/8/6/5/9, a true zero has probability on the order of 3e-4 under Poisson, and the zero is total — including larceny, which is the offense that carries essentially all of a commuter-campus Part-I count. The countervailing fact is the 12-month NIBRS batch header, but a header is an administrative months field, not a measurement of incidents, and SRS records only 1 month for 2024, contradicting the claim of full-year coverage.

rulings.detail: Void the zero; set 2024 missing and fill from own history, which is live and within the 2-year window: 2022 NIB 7/12mo and 2023 NIB 8/12mo give a fill near 8. Absolute stakes are small; the point is to stop a false structural zero being written onto the Palestine village place footprint. If the escalation budget allows, the confirming check is whether the 2024 NIBRS submission carries twelve explicit zero-report month flags or twelve headers with no incident segments.
rulings.rationale: Unlike the decaying cases, Palestine's post-transition level was flat and credible — 7 then 8 (about 600/100k for ~1,200 people) — and then stepped to exactly zero in all seven categories. From a stable lambda of 7.5 a zero year is a P=0.0006 event, roughly 1 in 1,800; against that, a header-continues/incidents-stop feed break is a mechanism this very batch demonstrates repeatedly. The 12-month NIBRS header is a submission envelope and cannot distinguish twelve zero-reports from twelve empty batches, and SRS offers nothing (0 at 1 month, statistically uninformative).

rulings.detail: Do not resolve on this packet. Two live hypotheses give opposite verdicts: (a) an operating 1,094-person village PD that genuinely recorded no Part-I offence in 2023 and 2024 (true zero), or (b) an Illinois NIBRS onboarding that registered 12-month batch headers while carrying no incident data (hollow feed). Resolving evidence needed: whether the 2023-2024 NIBRS submissions contain ANY Group A/Group B incidents of any type (drug, DUI, simple assault, vandalism). A feed with non-Part-I incidents but zero Part-I is a genuine zero; a feed with literally no incidents of any kind is hollow. Meanwhile: do NOT fill from own history — the last real report is 2020 and it fails the within-2-years rule, so any fill would be fabrication off a 2018 value.
rulings.rationale: The agency is NOT dormant — ROSTER2024 carries it as an active City agency with is_nibrs True, and a disbanded department does not file 12-month NIBRS batch headers, which rules out the structural-zero reading. But unlike the Hamilton Village case in this same batch, Norris City has NO independent lane to test the zero against: its NIBRS feed has never once carried a positive count (first row 2023, zero; 2024, zero), SRS has shown 0 months for four straight years (2021-2024), and the last positive anywhere is 2020. The 2018 full year of 19 argues against a true zero, but it predates a complete two-year submission blackout and a 10% population decline, so it cannot settle 2024. RESIDUAL DOUBT, record don't patch: the zero terminates a monotone annualized decline (31 / 16 / 16 / 10.5 / 6.9 / 0) and the all-zero vector makes the composition test inapplicable, so a phantom auto-zero-report feed cannot be excluded. Class-level follow-up: check whether municipal place 4854216 at w=1 exclusive is a coverage hole — a PD gone dark to the Upshur County sheriff produces a technically-true ORI zero plus a real geographic hole.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 FBI submission record shows 12 NIBRS months, not the 0-2 months that defines publication-without-submission, so the printed zero rests on a real full-year submission rather than a default label. Month coverage improved from 7mo (2023) to 12mo (2024) while content went to zero, which reads more like an agency that submitted more and found nothing than like a feed dying. For a town of 1,196 whose last two annualized levels were ~10.5 and ~6.9, a zero year is physically attainable, though it sits well below the 2021 full-12-month level of 16 — hence medium, not high.

rulings.detail: The printed zero is unusable; mark 2024 missing and fillable. Fill from own history — 2023 = 20 at 12mo in BOTH lanes (a clean, unambiguous full year, well inside the within-2-years rule); the 2018-2023 median is 21.5. Recommend ~20-21. EST2024=0 observed deletes a real agency's full year from a w=1 exclusive municipal footprint.
rulings.rationale: The deciding fact is the lane-month contradiction: NIB claims a 12-month 2024 while SRS — the only lane that can record months — records ZERO months, which is the signature of twelve NIBRS zero-report headers filed without any Return-A data, not of twelve measured months. Norwich's own record has no precedent for it: 2018-2023 run 15/14/23/29/28/20 with the SRS lane recording 10-12 months of actual data every single year, and 2023 specifically shows NIB 20/12mo + SRS 20/12mo. Against the agency's own lambda of ~20, a genuine full-year zero has probability e^-20, about 2e-9. The packet's 'DECISIVE PROVENANCE' claim that a 12-month NIBRS header proves a real submission is exactly the trap — a batch header can be twelve zero reports.

rulings.detail: Treat 2024 as partial, roughly 2-3 months believable (23 offences against a ~9.5/month historical run-rate implies ~2.4 months). EST2024=23 observed is not a defensible repair — it embeds an 80% phantom drop into the AL nonmunicipal remainder. Both lanes carry the same 23 at 12mo, so the ladder did NOT discard a larger submission; the fix is not lane reselection. Recommended basis: own-history fill from 2021-2023 (94, 112, 115; median 112), or a 12/2.5 month-ratio uplift of the observed 23 — both land near 100-115.
rulings.rationale: Crenshaw sits on a stable four-year plateau (2021:94, 2022:112, 2023:115) at essentially constant FBI population-served (10,190 -> 9,669), then drops to 23 in a single step with no scope change to explain it — flat population served rules out a jurisdictional narrowing. The 2024 mix (0/1/0/4/3/14/1) is a proportionally normal Part-I distribution scaled to about one fifth, which is the signature of month-truncation rather than offence-channel loss. Confidence is medium rather than high because the peer-rate arm did not fire (238/100k against a sheriff-band median of 627) and the composition is not internally broken, so a genuine sharp decline cannot be excluded from this packet alone.

rulings.detail: Keep EST2024 = 16 as observed. No repair needed. Recommend the c2 own-history arm be suppressed when the SRS submission record independently shows 11+ months, to stop this class of false positive.
rulings.rationale: All three lanes carry the same 16 and the SRS lane — the only one that counts literal months — reports 11, so the CIUS 12-month label is corroborated rather than assumed. The peer-rate arm did not fire: 693 per 100k for a 2,310-person town sits inside the normal range for its size band, meaning only the stale own-history median (65) drove the flag. Composition is intact across four classes (rape 2, agg assault 2, larceny 10, MVT 2) with larceny at 62% of the total, the normal share, not the single-category collapse that marks a partial feed. Burglary at 0 is unremarkable when the expected count is 2-3. Noted but not decisive: 16 happens to equal 65 x 3/12, which would be the arithmetic of a three-month partial — the 11-month SRS record is what rules that out.

rulings.detail: Structural zero — treat as missing, not as a reported zero. Zero believable months. Fill from own history, and prefer 2021 (179/178 at 12mo in BOTH lanes, the last clean year, pop-scaled 16,315 -> 16,235 = ~178) over 2022 (81 at NIB 12mo / SRS 8mo, itself depleted; annualizes to ~122). The 2020-2022 median is 111 and the peer anchor is 627.2/100k x 16,235 = 102. Recommend ~110-130 with the 102-178 spread recorded. EST2024=0 observed is indefensible.
rulings.rationale: NIB shows a 12-month 2024 while SRS records zero months — twelve zero-report headers, not twelve measured months — and as with Peach the ladder selected this lane on 'greater_month_coverage', i.e. on the strength of the artifact itself. Geneva County SO ran 242/142/111/178/81 across 2018-2022; against a lambda of roughly 80-180, a genuine full-year zero for a sheriff serving 16,235 people has probability around e^-160. The 2023 row is the tell that the feed died first, not the crime: NIB 0 at only 2 months with SRS at 0 months, and then 2024 claims coverage rose from 2 months to 12 while output stayed at zero — coverage and output moving in opposite directions is a filing artifact, never a crime signal. The agency's own 2019 line shows the same pattern in miniature (NIB 0/2mo alongside a real SRS 142/12mo).

rulings.detail: Do not keep 47 as observed. Believable coverage is roughly 3-4 months (47 vs the 2022-2023 level of 158-199). Refill from own recent history: 2023 = 158 at 12mo is inside the 2-year window and 2022 = 199, giving a hist_median fill of ~158; annualizing 47 x 12/4 gives ~141, which converges. EST2024 = 47 [observed] is NOT defensible. All three lanes carry 47, so no larger complete submission was discarded.
rulings.rationale: After a broken pre-2021 feed (10-12 total offences in 2018-2020 for a 5,800-person city), this agency came onto NIBRS in Feb 2021 and reported three solid full years — 138, 199, 158 — then dropped to 47 with nominal 12-month coverage in all three lanes. The composition is category-selectively hollow: agg assault holds at 11 (23% of the total, roughly double the normal index share) while burglary falls to 5 and MVT to 1, i.e. the violent side survived and the property side collapsed, which is a partial feed rather than a crime decline. The peer arm's silence is not exculpatory — the 1,096.9 per 100k median is national, whereas Monroeville's own 2022 rate was ~3,430 per 100k, so 829 per 100k is still a two-thirds cut against its actual level.

rulings.detail: Structural zero — treat the whole 2024 agency-year as missing (and 2023 likewise, same signature). Fill the full seven-offence vector as a unit from the last credible full years (2021 471, 2022 301) or from the sheriff 25-50k peer rate 706/100k x 41,418 = ~292, preserving a realistic offence mix. The current EST2024 is NOT defensible: 0/0/0/0/0/219.6/0 fabricates a jurisdiction where 100% of Part-I is larceny and zero of everything else, by filling one offence from hist_median while leaving six at observed zero — exactly the per-offence lane mixing the per-agency-year rule was meant to end.
rulings.rationale: A sheriff serving 41,418 people cannot record zero murders, rapes, robberies, assaults, burglaries, larcenies and MVTs across a full year; the peer floor is 706/100k and its own 2018-2022 record is 595/438/253/469/301. The 12-month NIBRS batch header is a submission envelope, not incident data — an RMS that stops exporting incidents while headers keep flowing produces exactly this, and SRS confirms 0 months on the other lane. 2023 carries the identical zero, so the feed has been dead two years.

rulings.detail: Keep 140 as observed; EST2024 (observed x7) is defensible. Add a watch flag only, no repair. All three lanes carry the identical 140/12mo so nothing larger was discarded by the ladder — the multi-lane hint is a non-issue here.
rulings.rationale: The instructed composition test passes: 0/9/2/29/20/76/4 is a complete, proportionate mix (burglary 20 against larceny 76, ratio 0.26; agg assault 29; rape 9), not the class-dropout signature of a partial feed. The rate is 1,725/100k against a peer median of 1,097 for local_police in the 5-10k band — above the floor, which is why only the c2 own-history arm fired. The 305->140 halving is large but both endpoints sit in credible ranges for Jackson County AR, and the NIBRS batch header reports 12 months. Only MVT (4, ~49/100k) is soft, not enough to overturn.

rulings.detail: Do not keep 1 as observed. Effective coverage is zero to one month — treat the agency-year as a non-report. Refill from own history: 2022 = 107 and 2023 = 88 are both full 12-month NIBRS years and 2023 is inside the 2-year window, so a hist_median fill of ~97.5 is the defensible repair. EST2024 = 1 [observed] is NOT defensible. Before filling, check whether Hanford's incidents were submitted under a neighbouring CHP area ORI in 2024 (Visalia/Porterville are the adjacent Central Valley offices) — if they migrated, filling would double count.
rulings.rationale: A CHP area office that reported 107 and 88 Part-I equivalents in 2022-2023 reporting exactly one offence — a single motor vehicle theft — under a 12-month batch header is the canonical dead-feed-behind-a-compliant-header pattern; CHP does not stop recording stolen and recovered vehicles on state highways. The sibling offices in this same batch (Visalia 314, Porterville 140, both MVT-dominated) establish what a live CHP area office's 2024 vector looks like, and 0/0/0/0/0/0/1 is not it. The missing FBI population makes the peer arm structurally blind here, so the own-history arm at 1.0% of baseline is the whole case — and at that magnitude it is decisive without needing a rate.

rulings.detail: Keep 136 for 2024; EST2024 [observed x7] is defensible as-is. Do not apply the own-history collapse arm to this ORI: its caseload is episodic rather than trended (611 -> 1,934 -> 2,279 -> non-report -> 1,636 -> 75 -> 136), so an own-history median is not a valid baseline and the 8.3%-of-median figure is an artifact of the metric. Peer-rate comparison is structurally impossible here (FBIpop = 0 for all years) and its absence is not evidence in either direction. Recommend downstream carry this as observed-but-volatile rather than flagged. Note separately that a railroad ORI on 06:statewide_overlap_layer may double-count with LAPD/LASD for the same rail-yard incidents — a jurisdictional-overlap issue, not a reporting-completeness one.
rulings.rationale: The composition test passes rather than fails: 0/0/0/1/91/44/0 is burglary-dominant, which is exactly the correct signature for a railroad police agency working container and rail-car break-ins, and zero murders, rapes, robberies and vehicle thefts on rail right-of-way with no residential population is expected rather than suspicious. This is the opposite of the Florida pathology in this batch, where violent counts collapse to zero while larceny carries the total in jurisdictions that must have violent crime. Coverage is stable across the whole record — months_reported is 12 in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023 and 2024, so the variation lives in the counts and not in the feed — and 2024 rose from 2023 (75 -> 136) rather than decaying toward zero, which is inconsistent with a dying partial feed. Roster nibrs_start 2025-01-01 confirms the agency was SRS-only in 2024, so no transition artifact is in play; confidence is capped at medium only because the 2022-to-2023 step is very steep.

rulings.detail: Keep 68 as observed; do not fill. Any own-history fill would be fabrication — sibling CHP area offices swing roughly 3x year over year in both directions. Rule note for downstream: the c2 own-history arm should not fire alone on FBIpop=0 state/special-jurisdiction ORIs (4,133 of 18,728 2024 ORIs), because the peer arm is structurally blind to them and no second test exists. Same footprint defect as the CA00199 block — a Shasta-county command smeared to 06:statewide_overlap_layer instead of its actual patrol area.
rulings.rationale: Composition is type-correct and it is the only affirmative test available here: 63 motor vehicle thefts and 5 larcenies with nothing else, matching the MVT-dominant Part-I profile CHP area offices produce (compare CHP Oakland at 385 MVT of 444). The FBI publishes no population for this ORI, so no peer-rate check exists and its absence carries no information either way. Sibling CHP offices in the same state and lane swing comparably in both directions in 2024 — Hayward 622→207 is a 67% fall, Oakland 259→444 a 71% rise — so a 189→68 step is inside the class distribution rather than anomalous. Only the own-history arm fired, and slope alone is not evidence.

rulings.detail: Treat 2024 as partial — at most about 1 month believable (7 offences against a ~7.5/month baseline). EST2024=7 observed is not defensible. Note the SRS lane's 7mo label is also unreliable: 7 offences over a claimed 7 months annualizes to 12, still an order of magnitude below baseline, so a month-ratio uplift is the wrong repair shape. Recommended basis: own-history fill from the last clean full years 2021-2022 (95, 86; ~90). Explicitly exclude 2023 from the baseline — its 37 at NIB 10mo / SRS 9mo is itself degraded and is where the break begins, so 2023 should be re-examined alongside 2024.
rulings.rationale: Three larcenies and one burglary for an entire year is not a possible measurement for a sheriff's office with 15,788 population served — that is a larceny rate of 19/100k against rural-sheriff norms in the hundreds. The all-offence rate of 43.2/100k is 6.9% of the sheriff-band peer median (627.2) and 7.4% of the agency's own 2018-2023 median of 95, with FBI population served flat across the entire period (15,884 -> 15,788), which rules out any scope narrowing. This is a long-standing NIBRS agency (nibrs_start 1997), so the collapse beginning in 2023 is a new feed break, not a transition artifact. Both the dual screen and the composition check agree.

rulings.detail: FLAG, do not auto-fill. This is a content-depleted feed beginning in 2023, NOT a months-partial, so no uplift applies (the batch headers really are 12 months). If a repair is made, it must come from the pre-2023 own-history level — 2018-2022 median 203, pop-scaled to 16,379 gives ~195 — which means the fill window has to reach past 2023, since the within-2-years rule would otherwise anchor on the equally suspect 2023 value of 42. Honest counter-evidence on the record: SRS carries 10 months WITH data in 2024 and 12 in 2023, and the 2024 mix is internally coherent, so this should be confirmed with CT DESPP / Wolcott PD (RMS or NIBRS-extract change at end of 2022) before any value is written.
rulings.rationale: The break is a cliff, not a decay — 194 (2022) to 42 (2023) to 33 (2024) — and a one-step 78% drop between two years both labelled 12 months in all three lanes is a feed-content change, not a crime trend; a smooth slope would have been the weaker signal, this is the stronger one. At 33/16,379 = 198.0 per 100k the agency sits at 14.9% of the peer median and roughly one sixth of its own 2018-2022 level of ~1,240/100k, which is outside the plausible support for any fully-reporting 16k-population municipal PD, including affluent New England suburbs. Unlike Sedro-Woolley in this same batch, whose 694/100k is ordinary, Wolcott's level is not reachable by a real decline. I am withholding a confident repair because the SRS-months test cannot detect content depletion behind an intact monthly header, so the mechanism is inferred rather than measured.

rulings.detail: Interim: keep 291 as observed — no repair is defensible. Do NOT apply partial-year uplift (SRS records 12 MEASURED months, not an assumed 12) and do NOT fill from own history (the 'baseline' is effectively the single year 2023). Escalate the ORI's identity and footprint instead, which is the real defect: roster-absent in 2024, no FBI population, agency_type 'unknown', name truncated to 'UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT', no county or place, and an 11:statewide_overlap_layer footprint at w=1 smearing a federal agency's mass across all of DC. Hypothesis to test (hedged, not established): the 'VA' ORI stem suggests Dept. of Veterans Affairs police filing under one DC ORI — if that composite spans facilities outside DC, the footprint is wrong at national scale and the 996->291 step likely reflects which facilities fed the composite, not crime.
rulings.rationale: Both 2023 (996) and 2024 (291) are SRS at 12 measured months, so none of the known artifacts fires: not BLANK-AS-ZERO (no publication lane involved, months are measured), not partial-month, not composition. The 2024 mix 0/6/0/13/10/252/10 is coherent and complete for a federal medical/campus force at 87% larceny with no missing stream, so the change is a uniform level shift rather than a feed gap. But the baseline is one usable year (2022 was 6mo, 2021 1mo, 2020 0mo) and the ORI's coverage is unresolved, so I cannot certify that 996 and 291 measure the same footprint — that underdetermination, not the count, is what needs a human.

rulings.detail: This one needs no estimate at all — it is a pure lane-selection error, and it is the cleanest demonstration in the batch. A genuine full-year FBI submission exists in the panel: SRS 1,040 at 12mo, tier high, vector 3/21/9/205/147/616/39, which is 88% of the 2023 full year (1,182) and 82% of 2022 (1,269) — a normal year-over-year decline for a 37,318-population city. The ladder discarded it in favour of SPUB 31 (0/9/0/1/3/16/2) solely because 'publication_lane_standing' outranks measured FBI lanes and SPUB rows are assigned months_reported=12 / tier high / weight 1.0 by assumption (artifact 2). Set 2024 = SRS 1,040 as observed. The current EST2024 of 898.9 is NOT defensible on two counts: it fabricates (trend_log_linear x3) when a real observation is sitting in the panel, and it retains four fragment values as 'observed' (murder 0, rape 9, robbery 0, MVT 2) for a city that reported 3 murders and 39 MVTs in the SRS lane the same year.
rulings.rationale: The packet explicitly asks whether the ladder discarded a larger equally-complete submission in favour of the small one, and here it demonstrably did — SRS 1,040 at a real 12 months lost to SPUB 31 at an assumed 12 months. The SPUB vector is self-evidently a fragment: 0 murders, 0 robberies and 1 aggravated assault for a 37k city, 3.0% of the FBI lane's own total for the identical agency-year. This is the highest-severity finding in the batch because the fix requires no imputation and because the same ladder ordering is corrupting Pembroke Pines and Homestead by the same mechanism.

rulings.detail: Reject the SPUB 7. 2024 = 248 from the SRS 12-month submission (0/12/4/51/47/125/9), taken as a full year with no uplift. EST2024=7 is not defensible. Rule-level fix: a state-publication row assigned months=12 by assumption must not outrank a genuine 12-month FBI submission when its total is a small fraction of it — the same FDLE-2024 token-row pattern hits Springfield, Lynn Haven and Pembroke Park in this batch alone.
rulings.rationale: The ladder discarded a larger, equally complete submission: SRS carries 248 at 12 months with a full balanced mix, consistent with 2020-2023 (305, 262, 256) and a rate of 2,606/100k for this Panama City suburb, while the FDLE row prints 0/1/0/0/2/4/0 = 7 (73.6/100k, 6.7% of peers). The SPUB row wins only because state publications carry no period field and get months=12/tier-high/weight-1.0 by assumption (artifact 2). With nibrs_start 2025-01-01, the agency's 2024 FDLE record is a transition-period stub, not a measurement.

rulings.detail: Two stacked errors. (1) Reject the SPUB 6. (2) 2024 = 166 from SRS, taken as a FULL YEAR — the months_reported=1 label is corrupt and the 12/1 annualization must be explicitly suppressed, or the panel gets 1,992 offences (9,113/100k) for a quiet Panama City suburb. Same corrupt 1mo label sits on 2023's 185, so apply the fix to both years. EST2024=6 is not defensible.
rulings.rationale: The SRS 2024 row 1/4/3/22/18/112/6 = 166 is a complete, balanced full-year mix at 759/100k, sitting squarely inside this agency's own full-year history (2018 230, 2019 339, 2020 215) and well under the 1,327/100k peer median for the 10-25k band — so the value is a year, not a month, and the period field is wrong. The FDLE row 0/1/0/0/1/3/1 = 6 (27.4/100k, 2.1% of peers) wins only through the months=12-by-assumption rule applied to state publications with no period field. nibrs_start 2025-01-01 marks 2024 as an FL transition-year stub.

rulings.detail: This is a lane-selection failure, not a crime fact. The ladder discarded a larger, genuinely complete submission: SRS Return-A 112 at 12 MEASURED months (0/3/0/14/9/83/3) in favour of an FDLE state-publication row of 2 (0/0/0/0/0/2/0) whose 12-month label is the pipeline's no-period-field assumption (artifact 2). EST2024 should be 112, sourced from srs_return_a_annual; the current EST2024=2 is indefensible and deletes ~98% of a real agency's crime. Corroboration that the SPUB row is empty by construction: ROSTER2024 gives nibrs_start = 2025-01-01, so Parker was still SRS-only through 2024 and Florida's NIBRS-derived publication has essentially no data for it. RULE GAP TO CLOSE: _drop_state_publication_non_reports only catches ALL-ZERO SPUB rows on zero SRS months; extend it to drop any SPUB row that is a tiny fraction (<10-20%) of a same-year FBI submission with full measured month coverage.
rulings.rationale: SRS 112 is internally consistent with Parker's own record (2019: 121, 2022: 96, 2023: 152) and with its peer band — 2198/100k against a 1096.9 median for a low-income Panhandle city of 5,096, roughly double peers, matching its long-run position. The SPUB 2 has a single larceny and nothing else across all seven categories, which is not a crime pattern but an absent feed. The single decisive fact is nibrs_start 2025-01-01: the state publication lane could not have carried Parker's 2024 offences, so its near-zero row is a structural artifact of the FL NIBRS transition, and publication_lane_standing let it outrank a measured full-year FBI submission.

rulings.detail: Do not keep 411. This is an offense-truncated feed, not a time-truncated one, so NO month-count uplift can repair it — the NIB vector 0/0/0/4/13/349/25 has murder, rape and robbery all at zero for a 175,757-population city while larceny carries 87% of the total. State how many months are believable: none cleanly; the roster's nibrs_start 2024-10-01 contradicts the NIB '12mo' label and implies at most 3 NIBRS months, and SRS says 8mo, and SPUB assumes 12 — all three lanes are the same broken feed with different labels. Own-history fill is NOT permitted: the last real full year is 2020 (2,704) and 2021, 2022 and 2023 are all SRS 0/0mo non-reports, so there is no real report within 2 years. Fill from peers (FL local_police, 100k-1M band) or from the 2020 anchor with a state trend adjustment, and flag the whole 2021-2024 block as a four-year hole.
rulings.rationale: Burglary at 14 alongside larceny at 359 in a city of 175,757 is the exact COMPOSITION-OVER-SLOPE signature — expected burglary for this size is roughly 400-600 and expected agg assault 400-600 against a reported 8. Both screen arms fired (own history 11.3%, peer rate 9.2% of the median), and the reported 233.8 per 100k against a peer median of 2,548.5 is not attainable by any real municipal police agency of this size. EST2024 keeping 411 as [observed x7] is the worst outcome available: it silently inserts a 176k-population city into the national panel at a tenth of its true level and drags the Broward County and Florida aggregates down without leaving a trace.

rulings.detail: Reject the SPUB 1 (a single burglary); set 2024 missing. Fill anchored on the agency's OWN established rate, not the peer median: last credible full year is 2020 SRS 230 (3,376/100k) against a band peer median of 1,097 — a peer fill would land near 75 and understate this commercial enclave threefold. Recommend own-rate anchor 230 trended on the Broward/FL 2020-2024 path (~160-230). Two caveats for downstream: the 2-year recency rule currently blocks that own-history path and needs an exception for agencies whose established rate is far off the peer median; and before filling, confirm Broward SO is not already carrying this town's calls, or the mass will double-count.
rulings.rationale: The FBI lane shows 0 months submitted in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024, so there has been no FBI submission for four years; the only 2024 value is an FDLE row of 1 offence that survived the all-zero drop rule solely because it is 1 rather than 0. One Part-I offence for a 6,812-person town with an own history of 336/267/230 is 14.7/100k, 1.3% of peers — not a measurement. Because the underlying coverage is zero months, no uplift can rescue it; the year has to be missing.

rulings.detail: Do not accept 26 as a complete 2024. The FBI submission record for FL0063800 in 2024 is SRS 0 total at 0 MONTHS — no submission exists. The SPUB 26 carries months_reported=12 only by the pipeline's no-period-field assumption (artifact 2). At most ~2-3 months of the FDLE feed are believable (26/125 = 21% of the 2021-2023 baseline). EST2024=26 observed is NOT defensible. Because a partial-year value on an unmeasured period cannot be safely uplifted, treat 2024 as missing/fillable and base it on the last full-coverage own-year (2022 NIB/SRS 125 at 12mo), i.e. ~120-130. Two secondary defects to record: (a) the SITUATION text says FBI publishes no population while the panel shows a flat imputed 8046 for all seven years — the peer-rate arm was blinded on a false premise; (b) the crosswalk footprint is 12:statewide_overlap_layer despite plc57425 (Southwest Ranches town) being known. Alternative worth checking before filling: Southwest Ranches is contract-policed, so if 2024 crime migrated to the contracting provider's ORI the right answer is superseded/treat-as-missing with NO fill — filling would then double-count.
rulings.rationale: This is the BLANK-AS-ZERO pattern one step up: a state publication printing a full-year-labelled figure for an agency whose FBI submission record is zero months. The decay 2022 (125 at 12mo) -> 2023 (53 at 5mo) -> 2024 (26 on 0 FBI months) is a feed dying, not crime falling. The offense mix confirms it — 0 murder / 2 rape / 0 robbery / 0 agg assault / 2 burglary / 20 larceny / 2 MVT: agg assault and robbery both empty in an 8k-population jurisdiction while larceny carries the total is a category-holed partial feed. Confidence is medium only because the contract-policing alternative (mass moved to another ORI) would change the repair from fill to no-fill.

rulings.detail: Treat 2024 as a structural non-report and discard all seven SPUB values. The FBI submission record for FL0130500 in 2024 is SRS 0/0mo with no NIBRS row (roster nibrs_start 2025-01-01) — the agency submitted nothing at all — so a 50-offense FDLE row cannot be a full year for an 82,094-population city. Own-history fill IS permitted: the last real full year is 2022 (2,589), within the 2-year window, so fill the entire vector from the 2022 level and split. The current EST2024 of 2,223.5 is right in magnitude but the vector is not defensible: it keeps murder=0 and rape=7 as 'observed' from the fragment and fabricates only the other five, so Homestead enters the panel with zero homicides in 2024 (it runs roughly 5-10/yr) next to a full-year larceny of 1,402. PIPELINE GAP: _drop_state_publication_non_reports keys on SPUB == 0 exactly; this row is SPUB == 50 sitting on a 0-month FBI year and therefore evades the rule. Re-key the rule on 'SPUB total implies an implausible fraction of own history or of the FBI lane', not on equality with zero.
rulings.rationale: Both screen arms fired hard — 1.8% of the own-history median and 3.1% of the peer median at 60.9 per 100k against 1,953.7 — and the composition confirms a fragment rather than low crime, with murder 0 and motor vehicle theft 0 in an 82k city alongside burglary 5 and larceny 27. The decisive fact is provenance rather than magnitude: an agency with zero months submitted to the FBI has no full-year measurement in existence, so the FDLE row is a partial upload printed without a period field and assigned months_reported=12 by pipeline assumption (artifact 2). Note also that 2021 and 2023 are themselves 0-month non-reports, so this agency has an intermittent record and the 2022 anchor is the only recent real full year.

rulings.detail: Treat as a non-report, not a partial — there is nothing to uplift. Zero believable months. Fill must come from own history (2019 190/12mo, 2020 194/12mo, pop-scaled -> ~195); a peer fill is CATASTROPHICALLY wrong here (702.6/100k x 1031 = 7 offences) because Medley is a ~1,000-resident Miami-Dade industrial/warehouse district whose own record implies ~19,000/100k from daytime population. The within-2-years own-history rule blocks the correct fill, so escalate the fill window. rulings.detail: Do not accept 17 as a complete year. The FDLE row covers at most ~7 months and is offense-depleted within those months, so neither the observed 17 nor a 12/7 uplift (~29) is usable. rulings.detail: Treat SPUB 67 as ~1 month of coverage (2 at the outside), not a 12-month year. Mark 2024 non-observed and fillable; EST2024=67 observed is indefensible. rulings.detail: structural_zero_treat_as_missing — 0 believable months. rulings.detail: This is a lane-selection defect, not agency behaviour. The 2024 value should be the SRS 560 at 12 MEASURED months; EST2024=111 is indefensible. Systemic fix (this is the highest-value item in the batch): publication_lane_standing must not let a period-less SPUB row, whose months_reported=12 / tier high / weight 1.0 is assigned by assumption (artifact 2), outrank an FBI lane carrying a MEASURED 12-month count. Demote SPUB below any lane with a real months field.

The ladder promoted the assumed-complete publication row over a measured complete submission purely on lane standing, deleting 449 offenses from a 27,462-person city.

rulings.detail: Accept 2024; EST2024=186 is defensible, though I would prefer the FBI 12-month NIBRS/SRS value of 182 on provenance grounds (measured months vs assumed) — the 2% difference is immaterial either way. The screen fired against a garbage baseline: the '2021-2023 median 1172' rests on a single wild SRS year sandwiched between 0 (2021, 1 month) and 92 (2023, 11 months), so the collapse is an artifact of the baseline, not of 2024. The real defect on this ORI is the footprint, not the count: an airport police department is carried at 12:statewide_overlap_layer w=1 (marked [mini_second_pass/reviewed]), smearing its mass across the whole of Florida. It should be a non-exclusive overlap on the airport polygon within Hillsborough County / Tampa.
rulings.rationale: Three lanes land independently at 182-186 for 2024, two of them (NIBRS and SRS) at 12 MEASURED months, so this is a complete full-year submission rather than a relabeled partial — the opposite configuration from the other FL cases in this batch. The offense mix 0/0/1/2/2/165/12 — 91% larceny, 12 MVT, near-zero violent and burglary — is exactly the coherent profile of a facility with no resident population, so the composition test passes cleanly (contrast Vero Beach, where MVT=0 fails it). 2024 is the agency's first clean full NIBRS year (nibrs_start 2023-07-01) and is consistent with 2023's 92-in-11-months once the mid-year start is accounted for.

rulings.detail: Not a partial-month case — the NIBRS header really is 12 months — but an offense-stream gap, so partial-year uplift does not apply. Mark 2024 non-observed; EST2024=58 is indefensible. Do NOT fill from 2023 (81 at 11mo) even though it is inside the 2-year window: 2023 is itself degraded and filling from it propagates the defect. Anchor on the last uncompromised full year, 2020 SRS 284, cross-checked against a peer-band fill (1327.2/100k x 18,049 = ~240); the two agree at ~240-285, so either is defensible. Rule addition: a within-window own-history year that itself fails a composition check must be excluded as a fill source.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 vector is 0/2/1/5/5/43/0 — motor vehicle theft at exactly zero across a full 12 months in an 18,049-person Florida city, where the state rate implies roughly 30-40, and burglary 5 against larceny 43 is far off any normal ratio. That is the COMPOSITION-OVER-SLOPE signature: specific offense streams are missing from the NIBRS feed even though the batch header reports 12 complete months, so a 12mo label cannot be read as complete coverage here. The SPUB 58 is the same vector plus two larcenies, so it is a copy of the defective feed rather than independent corroboration, and the agency's last uncompromised year is 2020 at 284 — four years back and outside the own-history fill window.

rulings.detail: At most 6 months believable, and even those are under-covered. Mark 2024 non-observed; EST2024=93 is indefensible. Preferred repair: own-history fill from 2022 (465) and 2023 (439), both real 12-month NIBRS/SRS years inside the 2-year window, giving ~452. Treat the 6-month uplift (93 x 2 = 186) as a hard floor only, not the estimate — motor vehicle theft at exactly 0 over a nominal half-year in a 22,871-person city shows the six months are themselves missing offense streams, which is why the uplift under-shoots history by ~55%.
rulings.rationale: The SPUB vector 1/11/2/23/11/45/0 is the same data as the NIB/SRS vector 1/7/2/23/11/45/0 — identical in six of seven offenses — so the SPUB's '12 months' is the same 6-month submission relabeled by the pipeline's period-less assumption, not an independent full year; it cannot corroborate a feed it was derived from. The FBI lanes measure 6 months for 2024 against clean 12-month years in 2022 and 2023, so the feed broke mid-year. MVT=0 across that nominal half-year is an offense-stream gap stacked on top of the month gap, so month-ratio uplift alone will not restore the year.

rulings.detail: Do not accept 40 as complete. Believable coverage is roughly 2-3 months (40/215 of a full year = 2.2 months). Mark 2024 missing and fill at ~222-225 — reassuringly, two independent anchors converge: 2019 own full year 215 at pop 15,947 = 1,348/100k scaled to 2024 pop 16,715 gives ~225, and the peer anchor 1,327.2/100k x 16,715 gives ~222. IMPORTANT downstream guard: the within-2-years own-history rule will find the 2023 (7/5mo) and 2022 (13/4mo) rows and fill from garbage — those years must be excluded from the fill basis. EST2024=40 observed is not defensible.
rulings.rationale: The FBI records zero submitted months for 2024 (SRS 0/0mo); the sole 2024 row is a state-publication line whose 12mo/high/w=1 status is the pipeline's assumption for a table with no period field (artifact 2). The mix 0/3/0/2/5/30/0 carries MVT = 0 and burglary = 5 for a 16,715-population city — a partial feed, since MVT is the offense small agencies least often miss and would be expected at ~15-30. The agency has not filed a clean year since 2019 (20: 1mo, 21: 1mo, 22: 4mo, 23: 5mo) and nibrs_start is only 2023-05-01, so 40 is consistent with roughly two months of a still-stabilizing NIBRS feed. At 239.3/100k it sits at 18% of peers while its own 2019 full year was ~1,350/100k — the town did not change, the feed did.

rulings.detail: Treat 2024 as a non-report: zero months believable, mark missing rather than uplifting. EST2024=1 is not defensible. Own-history fill is barred (last real report 2020, four years back, fails the within-2-years rule), so 2024 must come from a peer/benchmark fill for FL local_police in the 5k-10k band — roughly 1096.9/100k x 5,941 = ~65, which also brackets its own 2018-19 level of 52-55.

The single FDLE-published larceny survived _drop_state_publication_non_reports only because the rule catches all-zero rows, not all-but-one; it is a near-miss on the existing guard, not evidence of a submission. One larceny and nothing else for a 5,941-person city against an own-history median of 52 is a token, and because it is published as complete it gets no uplift and stands as-is. A partial-year value this close to zero cannot be rescued by scaling regardless.

rulings.detail: Do NOT keep 3,772 as an observed full year. Mark FL0480000 2024 as partial/non-complete on all three lanes and correct the month labels: NIB should be 1 month (roster nibrs_start 2024-12-01), SPUB ~2 months, SRS <1 month. Best-grounded 2024 total is the December NIBRS fragment annualized: 1,804 x 12 = ~21,650, which lands on the 2022 full-year level of 21,130. The current EST2024 of 17,092 is right in magnitude but the vector is not defensible: it keeps murder=13 as 'observed' from a ~2-month SPUB fragment and splices it against six hist_median full-year values (larceny 10,126), producing an internally inconsistent record. Discard all seven 2024 observed values, or rebuild the whole vector from the December NIBRS month.
rulings.rationale: Three lanes claim to be the same agency's same complete year yet report motor-vehicle-theft of 439 (SPUB), 14 (NIB) and 2 (SRS) — a 31x spread that no full year can accommodate, so at most one is right and none is complete. NIB 1,804 is almost exactly one month at the historical rate (21,130/12 = 1,761) and the roster's nibrs_start of 2024-12-01 confirms a single NIBRS month mislabeled as 12mo. A 960k-population sheriff cannot fall 82% in one year while the composition breaks (SPUB burglary 320 against larceny 2,237), so this is fragment coverage, not a trend. Own record is already thin — 2021 and 2023 are 0-month non-reports and the last real full year is 2022 — so any own-history anchor is stale at exactly the 2-year boundary.

rulings.detail: At most 7 months believable, and under-covered within those. Mark 2024 non-observed; EST2024=139 is indefensible. Preferred repair: own-history fill from 2022 (516) and 2023 (457), both real 12-month NIBRS/SRS years inside the 2-year window, giving ~486. The 7-month uplift (139 x 12/7 = 238) is a floor only — it still sits at ~52% of 2023, so the seven months are themselves partial.

The FBI lanes measure 7 (NIBRS) and 6 (SRS) months for 2024, against clean 12-month years in 2022 (516) and 2023 (457). The ladder promoted an assumed-complete publication row over the measured partial submission it was derived from — the same FDLE defect as Fort Walton Beach and Vero Beach in this batch.

rulings.detail: Do not accept 37 as complete. Believable coverage is ~2 months (37/201 of a full year = 2.2 months; the FBI's own NIBRS row for 2024 is a 1-month stub). Best-supported repair in the whole batch: fill from own history at 2023 = 201 at 12mo, which is INSIDE the within-2-years rule, pop-scaled 11,194/10,909 -> ~206. Prefer this over the peer anchor (1,327.2/100k x 11,194 = 149), since Milton's own clean full years are 199 (2022) and 201 (2023). The only 2024 row is a state-publication line whose 12mo/high status is the pipeline's assumption for a table with no period field (artifact 2), and 37 is 18.4% of the agency's own 2023 full year.
