Unlike the other Florida cases here, this agency was a clean full reporter immediately before the gap (2022: 199/12mo, 2023: 201/12mo), so both the diagnosis and the fill are unusually well determined.

rulings.detail: Do not keep 46 as observed. Believable coverage is roughly 4 months (46 vs the 2021-2022 level of ~144). Refill from own recent history anchored on 2022 (144 at 12mo, within the 2-year window) with population growth applied (17,161 -> 18,169), giving ~150; annualizing 46 x 3 gives ~138 and a peer-rate fill gives ~241. Recommend the own-history route at ~140-150. EST2024 = 46 [observed] is NOT defensible. Note 2023 (102) is itself likely partial and should carry a soft flag. All three lanes carry 46, so no larger submission was discarded.
rulings.rationale: An 18,169-person Augusta-metro suburb reporting 5 burglaries, 30 larcenies and 1 motor vehicle theft for a full year is not a measurement — the larceny rate alone (165 per 100k) is about an eighth of any plausible suburban level, and 1 MVT next to Augusta is impossible. The population is rising (14,543 -> 18,169) while the count falls 200 -> 46, so the denominator is moving against the trend rather than explaining it, and the rate sits at 19.1% of the peer median. Composition confirms slope: the property side is hollowed out, so the smooth 200/190/147/145/141/102/46 decay is a decaying feed, not a decaying crime rate.

rulings.detail: Do not repair and do not certify. Hold the agency-year as low-confidence pending Grady's 2024 NIBRS monthly detail — specifically whether all twelve submitted months carry Group A incidents, or whether incidents cluster in roughly four months. If the months are populated, 63 stands as observed; if they cluster, treat as a ~4-month partial and uplift to ~180. Do not apply a peer fill either way: the peer arm did not fire.
rulings.rationale: The two decisive tests disagree and neither dominates. Composition passes — all seven categories are populated in proportions normal for a rural Georgia sheriff (burglary 19 / larceny 20 / MVT 11) — and the peer-rate arm did not fire at 399/100k, so against same-type same-size peers 63 is not an outlier. Against that, coverage broke and returned (12mo 2021 → 5mo 2022 → 0mo 2023 → 12mo 2024) and 63 is almost exactly 4/12 of the last comparable full year (182 x 4/12 = 61). A first year back after a total blackout is precisely where the 12mo label is least trustworthy, and nothing in the packet separates a truncated feed from a real decline.

rulings.detail: Do not let 37 stand. Treat the 2024 agency-year as unreliable/missing and fill from own history (2021-2023 median 130, or a trend fit through 102/131/130/111). Do NOT uplift by a 12/n month ratio — n would have to be back-derived from the baseline, which is circular. EST2024=37 observed is not a defensible output.
rulings.rationale: Four consecutive rock-stable full-year submissions (2020:102, 2021:131, 2022:130, 2023:111) then 37 — a 67% break with no population change (31,550 to 32,316) and no lane change. Both screen arms fired: 114.5 per 100k against a 706.2 sheriff peer median (16.2% of peers). The composition seals it: larceny 20 carries 54% of the year while burglary is 5 and aggravated assault is 3 for a 32k-population exurban Georgia county sheriff — 5 burglaries in a full year at that footprint is a feed that stopped, not a crime drop.

rulings.detail: Do not carry 46 as an observed full year; mark 2024 incomplete and fillable. Own 2022 full year (189, at the 2-year window boundary) and the peer rate (706.2/100k x 26,635 = 188) converge on ~188, which is a well-anchored fill target. EST2024=46 [observed] is not defensible. Also flag 2023 (41/12mo) as the same defect — the break is at 2022→2023, not at 2024, so repairing 2024 alone would leave a matching hole in the prior year.
rulings.rationale: The vector is broken rather than merely small: zero murders, zero rapes and zero robberies across a 26,635-person county remainder, with burglary 4 sitting below MVT 11 — an inversion rural sheriff jurisdictions do not produce. Violent offences are absent while property is present but thin, which is category-selective loss, not a uniformly quiet year. The peer arm fires at 24.5% of the sheriff-band median and the drop is from a genuine 12-month 2022 of 189. Both 2024 lanes carry the identical 46, so the ladder did not discard a larger submission.

rulings.detail: Structural zero — treat as missing, not as a reported zero. Zero believable months. Fill from own history but anchor on 2022 (131 at 12mo in BOTH lanes) rather than 2023: 2023's 68 carries NIB 12mo against SRS 7mo, so it is itself depleted and annualizes to ~117. Recommend ~125-131 (pop essentially flat, 13,309 -> 13,298). Note the peer anchor is much lower (627.2/100k x 13,298 = 83), so record the 83-131 spread; own history is the better anchor for a sheriff whose own full years ran 131-237. EST2024=0 observed is indefensible.
rulings.rationale: NIB shows a 12-month 2024 while SRS — the only lane able to record months — shows zero months, the zero-report-header fingerprint, and the selection reason 'greater_month_coverage' means the ladder picked the lane precisely on the strength of that fake coverage. Peach County SO ran 237/184/228/154/131 across 2018-2022 with full months in both lanes; against a lambda of roughly 130-230 a genuine full-year zero has probability on the order of e^-130, which is not a number any evidence in this packet can overcome. A sheriff's office serving 13,298 people in Georgia recording no murder, rape, robbery, assault, burglary, larceny or MVT for twelve months is not a crime fact. The 2023 step (68, with SRS at only 7 months) shows the feed was already failing a year before it went fully silent.

rulings.detail: Flag as suspect-complete. Do NOT apply a month-ratio uplift — the months here are real (SRS 12/12), so the defect is under-compilation inside a genuinely filed year, and 12/n scaling would be unjustified. If a value is substituted, anchor to the recent own-history level (2021:43, 2022:90, 2023:32 at 10mo = ~38 annualized; median ~43) and record the flag rather than silently overwriting, since a real small-agency staffing collapse is a live alternative explanation.
rulings.rationale: On a per-month basis 2024 runs 1.0/mo against 3.6/mo (2021), 7.5/mo (2022) and 3.2/mo (2023), so the break survives the months correction — it is a genuine drop in the reported rate, not a coverage artifact. The offense mix (9 larceny / 2 burglary / 1 agg assault) is normally shaped, but at n=12 that is exactly what a 4-month slice of a ~38/yr agency looks like, so the mix does not discriminate here. Working against the flag: SRS records a real 12 of 12 monthly Return-A submissions (not a CIUS default), and the peer-rate arm did not fire — which is why this is medium and not high. For a stable-population county seat of 2,628 with five prior full years at 43-149, a single-year fall to 12 is far more consistent with an agency that stopped compiling than with a 70% real crime drop.

rulings.detail: Keep EST2024 = 19 as observed. No repair. If a coverage concern remains it belongs to the sheriff-footprint question (the county's municipal PDs in Rock Rapids/George/Inwood are separate ORIs), not to a 2024 uplift.
rulings.rationale: Both lanes report 12 months for 2024 and SRS — the lane that can record a literal month count — agrees at 12, so there is no submission-record contradiction of the completeness label. Composition passes the stated diagnostic in the strong direction: burglary 7 against larceny 8, plus MVT 3 and one agg assault, is a balanced property mix, not the burglary-collapse-while-larceny-carries-everything signature of a partial feed. The 82-to-37-to-19 slide is smooth, and per COMPOSITION OVER SLOPE I give the slope no weight either way — it is the intact mix and the full month count that carry the ruling. 151 per 100k is 24% of the sheriff peer median, low but not extreme for the unincorporated remainder of a very rural northwest Iowa county.

rulings.detail: Keep 37 as observed for the 2024 level; EST2024 = 37 is defensible. Record two separate items that are NOT reasons to alter 2024: (a) the 2019 -> 2022 level break (134 -> 49, with 2021 a 0-month non-report) should be flagged in the trend series as a regime discontinuity, not smoothed; (b) the 2020 row is a genuine data conflict — CIUS 22 at 6 offense rows versus SRS 312 — and 312 is an outlier against every neighbouring year, so 2020 should be treated as unreliable in the history.
rulings.rationale: Unlike the other collapse cases here, 2024 is 87.1% of the 2021-2023 baseline: three consecutive full-coverage years at 49, 36, 37 is a stable settled level, and only the c1 arm anchored on the pre-2021 regime fires. The composition is coherent for the place — larceny 26 dominant, burglary 9, robbery 1, MVT 1 — with no hollowed category, and the zeros on murder/rape/agg assault are ordinary for a 13,200-person residential village with essentially no big-box retail. Western Springs is one of the lowest-crime municipalities in Illinois, which is exactly the situation the peer-rate floor cannot adjudicate on its own; the burden then falls on stability plus composition, and both pass.

rulings.detail: Keep EST2024 = 19 as observed for the 2024 agency-year. SEPARATE MULTI-YEAR ISSUE to route, not fixable by a 2024 uplift: the 2020-to-2021 level break (103/109/67 then 3/21/18/19) coincides with nibrs_start 2021-11-01 and drops the agency from ~1,150 per 100k — dead on the peer median — to ~200 per 100k, where it has held for four years. That is a suspected chronic NIBRS-transition coverage loss spanning 2021-2024; uplifting 2024 alone would create a false discontinuity against 2022 and 2023.
rulings.rationale: The c2 arm explicitly did not fire: 2024 is 97.4% of the agency's own 2021-2023 baseline of 19.5, so it is not anomalous within the current reporting regime — the c1 flag fired only against a stale six-year median dominated by the pre-transition SRS era. All three lanes agree at 19 with SRS independently recording 12 months. Composition passes the stated diagnostic strongly, spanning six of seven classes with burglary 5 against larceny 6, the healthy ratio rather than the larceny-carries-everything collapse. Rebuilding 2024 to the pre-2020 level of 67 would be fitting the result to a baseline the agency has not occupied since 2020.

rulings.detail: Do not keep 6 as observed; 2022 (0) and 2023 (1) should be flagged the same way. Effective coverage is at or near zero months despite the 12-month NIBRS header. Own-history fill is poisoned — the 2021-2023 baseline median is 0.5, and the last credible year (2020, SRS 104 at 12mo) is four years stale and fails the within-2-years rule — so the fill must be peer-based: the sheriff median of 593.1 per 100k on a served population of 5,617 gives ~33 offences. Flag the gap between that peer figure and the agency's own last-good level of ~100 for review. EST2024 = 6 [observed] is NOT defensible.
rulings.rationale: Larceny 0 alongside agg assault 4 inverts the normal rural-sheriff mix, where larceny is the dominant category — this agency carried 100, 97 and 104 total offences in 2018-2020, so a year with literally no larceny is a broken feed, not a low year. The break lands exactly on the Illinois NIBRS transition (nibrs_start 2020-12-01): SRS coverage was solid through 2020, then 2021 gives 4 at 5 months and 2022-2024 give 0, 1 and 6 under nominal 12-month NIBRS headers. The peer arm agrees at 16.5% of median, and the c2 arm's absurd '1200% of baseline' reading is itself the tell that the recent history is garbage rather than a usable anchor.

rulings.detail: Flag 2024 as not credible and flag 2022-2024 as a block — repairing 2024 alone against a 2021-2023 baseline of 12.5 just launders the same undercount. Own-history fill from 2022/2023 (17, 8) propagates the defect; the level must be re-derived from the pre-break regime (2018-2020 median ~95, i.e. ~2,200 per 100k) cross-checked against the peer band (929.7 per 100k x 4,230 = ~39). That 39-95 spread is wide and should be resolved deliberately, not asserted. EST2024=6 observed is not defensible.
rulings.rationale: The series steps 95/103/86 (2018-2020) to 17/8/6 (2022-2024) across a 2021 total non-report (SRS 0 at 0 months), with the break landing on nibrs_start 2022-01-01 — the Illinois NIBRS-transition signature. The 2024 mix is 3 aggravated assaults, 1 burglary, 2 larcenies for a city of 4,230: larceny at 2 where the pre-break years implied roughly 60-70 is a dead feed, and SRS records only 9 months against the CIUS-assumed 12. This ORI's CIUS lane is independently shown to be lossy — in 2020 it printed 44 with only 6 offense rows while SRS carried 86 at 12 months — and CIUS is the lane that won the ladder for 2024.

rulings.detail: credible_low_crime — keep EST2024 = 21. No repair. Add to a watchlist rather than a fill queue: if 2025 also lands far below 65, the year to re-examine is 2023 (the agency's first full NIBRS year, 65) rather than 2024.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 vector 0/1/0/1/5/13/1 is a textbook small-city mix — larceny at 62% of Part-I with every property class populated — so the composition test that catches partial feeds returns clean. The rate is 724/100k and the peer-rate arm did not fire; only the own-history arm did. All three lanes agree at 21 with 12mo headers and SRS at 11mo (uplift gives 23, immaterial), so the ladder discarded no larger or better-covered submission. The 65-to-21 drop is beyond Poisson noise and genuinely worth watching, but every completeness test available says measurement, and slope alone is explicitly not grounds to overturn a value.

rulings.detail: Do not carry 67 as an observed full year. The mechanism is a category-selective export/mapping defect, not month truncation, so a partial-year uplift is the WRONG repair — mark the agency-year unusable and fill instead. Own 2022 full year (206, inside the 2-year window) and the peer rate (1327.2/100k x 16,985 = 225) converge on ~206-225; fill at ~206. Also flag 2023 (68/9mo) as the same defect, since it appears first there. EST2024=67 is not defensible; all three lanes carry the identical 67, so lane choice is not the fault.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 vector is internally impossible: 7 rapes against 1 aggravated assault and 0 robberies in a 16,985-person city. Aggravated assault always vastly outnumbers rape in real Part-I data, so this is neither a low-crime year nor a uniform month-truncation — rape sits at roughly its expected level while agg assault, robbery and burglary land at 0-8% of expectation. That category-selective pattern points at the offense-code export rather than at coverage, and it appears first in 2023 (68/9mo) immediately after a clean 12-month 2022 of 206. The peer arm's silence at 29.5% of the band median does not rescue it, because the defect is in the mix, not the level.

rulings.detail: A genuine 3-month partial mislabeled complete, not a token report. Believable months: 3 (both NIB and SRS state months_reported=3). Correct repair is uniform annualization across all seven offenses: 612 x 12/3 = ~2,448, i.e. 4/16/11/106/67/305/103 x4 = 16/64/44/424/268/1220/412. That is 97% of the 2023 full year (2,514) and 113% of the 2021-2023 baseline median (2,162), confirming the multiplier. The current EST2024 of 1,527 is NOT defensible: it applied true_partial_month_ratio to larceny alone (305 -> 1,220) and left the other six offenses at 3-month values, yielding 62% of the true level and a vector where larceny is annualized and murder, robbery and burglary are not.
rulings.rationale: Both 2024 lanes carry months_reported=3 explicitly, so partial-year status is measured, not inferred — the defect is the 'published as complete' classification that suppressed the uplift. The 3-month mix is proportionate across all seven offenses with no category-specific hole, unlike the Florida cases in this batch where violent counts collapse to zero while larceny carries the total. This is the same root-cause bug as c-LA0170200-baton-rouge with a different offense annualized, which points at one fix rather than two.

rulings.detail: Keep 113 as observed; no fill or uplift is defensible. Attach a watch flag for the -71% three-year drift (392→330→250→113) so a further step down in 2025 gets re-examined, but do not let slope alone trigger a repair. EST2024=113 [observed] is the correct output.
rulings.rationale: Composition is the affirmative test and it passes: larceny 59 is 52% of the index, all seven categories are populated, and the mix is normal for a parish-remainder sheriff. The peer arm did not fire — 414/100k is roughly 59% of the ~706/100k sheriff-band median — so it is not deeply below same-type peers. Coverage is an unbroken 12-month NIBRS run across 2021-2024 with no gap or partial year, so this is not the returning-filer profile that makes a 12mo label suspect. That leaves only the slope, which under the composition-over-slope rule is not by itself evidence in either direction.

rulings.detail: This is not a token report — it is a clean 4-month partial that the pipeline labeled complete. Believable months: 4 (both NIB and SRS state months_reported=4 explicitly). Correct repair is uniform annualization across all seven offenses: 4,475 x 12/4 = ~13,425, i.e. 24/26/100/513/839/2214/759 x3 = 72/78/300/1539/2517/6642/2277. That lands at 94% of the 2021-2023 baseline median of 14,307, confirming the 4 months are genuine and complete. The current EST2024 of 4,523 is NOT defensible: it applied true_partial_month_ratio to murder alone (24 -> 72) and left the other six offenses at their 4-month values, producing a record where murder is at full-year scale and larceny is at one-third scale, and a total that is 34% of the true level.
rulings.rationale: Both 2024 lanes carry months_reported=4, so there is no ambiguity that this is a partial year — the only error is the 'published as complete' classification that suppressed the uplift. The 4-month offense mix 24/26/100/513/829/2214/759 is proportionate across all seven categories with no offense-specific hole, which distinguishes a genuine time-truncated feed from the broken-composition partial feeds elsewhere in this batch. Uniform annualization reproducing 94% of the three-year baseline is strong independent confirmation that 12/4 is the right multiplier.

rulings.detail: Flag 2024 as not credible; do not ship 8 as observed. If repaired, anchor to the post-2021 regime only (2021-2023 median ~18 / most recent 16), never to the pre-2021 level of 156. Separately and more importantly: flag the 2020->2021 step (156 -> 24, a 6.5x drop landing exactly on nibrs_start 2021-01-01) as a transition-induced regime break covering 2021-2024, so the whole stretch is reviewed rather than 2024 patched alone.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 offense mix is 6 burglaries against 1 larceny for a city of ~7,000 — an inverted ratio that no real full year produces, since larceny is the dominant Part-I category in every agency of this size; that is a broken feed, not a thin year. SRS records only 9 months while CIUS and NIBRS assert 12, and CIUS (the assumed-12mo, assumed-tier-high lane) is what won the ladder. Both screen arms fired, with 93.1 per 100k against a 1,096.9 peer median (8.5% of peers). The level break coinciding exactly with the NIBRS start date is the larger defect: the post-2021 baseline of 18 that makes 2024 look only halved is itself a depressed regime.

rulings.detail: Not a ladder error — NIB 8 at 12mo vs SRS 8 at 10mo is the same value; nothing larger was discarded. Even the most generous partial-month uplift (12/10 x 8 = 9.6) gets nowhere near a credible year, so this is not a partial-year case. EST2024=8 observed is not defensible. Repair basis: the last clean own-years are 2021 (130) and 2022 (112) at full coverage in both lanes, giving ~110-120; peer cross-check gives 929.7/100k x 4,872 = ~45 as a floor, so the own-history anchor is the better basis for a town with this long a record. As with Crook, 2023 (26 at NIB 12mo) is already defective and must be excluded from the own-history fill basis rather than used as the nearest 'real report'.
rulings.rationale: Lincoln ran 94-130 Part-I offences every year 2018-2022 with a stable population of ~4,870, then dropped to 26 and then 8 at unchanged full month coverage — 7.1% of its own median, which no genuine crime trend produces in a town whose population did not move. The 2024 mix is 0/0/0/0/1/6/1: six larcenies and nothing else across an entire year for a town with its own police department, i.e. 123/100k larceny against a national ~1,300. The break follows nibrs_start 2020-12-01 by two years, the classic post-transition RMS feed failure where the state program keeps stamping full months while incident content stops flowing. Both screen arms fired independently (7.1% of own baseline, 17.6% of peers).

rulings.detail: Do not carry 32 as an observed full year; mark 2024 incomplete and fillable. Own 2022 full year (157 CIUS / 158 NIB-SRS, inside the 2-year window) and the peer rate (1327.2/100k x 12,137 = 161) converge on ~158-161, so fill at ~160 — the convergence of two independent anchors makes that well-founded. Roughly 2-3 months of property reporting is the believable coverage. EST2024=32 [observed] is not defensible; all three lanes carry the identical 32, so lane choice is not the fault.
rulings.rationale: The offense mix is decisive: 14 larcenies in a growing 12,137-person I-35 exurb (expect 150-250) with a single motor vehicle theft, while agg assault at 11 is 34% of the index against a national share near 7%. Property is gutted and violent is intact, which is a partial feed rather than a quiet year. The peer arm fires at 19.9% of the band median, and the run 258/188/256/181/158/72/32 across nominally 12-month years is the textbook smooth decay of a dying feed — which the composition-over-slope rule says must not be read as a genuine trend.

rulings.detail: token_report_treat_as_partial — about 3-4 months of content is believable. Mark 2024 missing and fill from own 2021-2023 full years (98/61/54, median ~61); cross-check against the sheriff peer band (627.2/100k x 16,752 = ~105), which is higher, so own-history is the conservative basis. EST2024=16 observed is indefensible, and a month-ratio uplift is insufficient on its own: 16 x 12/9 = 21, still a third of the own-history level.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 vector 0/0/0/8/2/6/0 is inverted — agg assault (8) exceeds larceny (6), burglary is 2, MVT is 0 — for a sheriff covering ~16,750 people. A functioning rural-sheriff feed is larceny-dominant; agg-assault dominance with MVT at zero is the signature of a feed carrying violent/arrest incidents while property offences fail to flow. Both screen arms fired: 26% of own history and 14% of the peer-band median. The 2021-2023 NIBRS years (98/61/54) ran clean on the same feed that started 2020-11-01, so 2024 is a break in a working feed, not a level shift.

rulings.detail: Not a ladder error — NIB and SRS both carry 40 at 12 months. The defect is inside the submission: the larceny feed is broken. Treat 2024 as materially incomplete; month-ratio uplift does not apply because coverage is genuinely full. EST2024=40 observed is not defensible. Repair basis: the 2021-2023 own-history baseline median of 128 for the Rice County unincorporated remainder (2021: 146, 2022: 128 both at full coverage), cross-checked against the sheriff band. Extend the review to 2023 as well — 75 at 12mo is already ~59% of baseline, so the degradation begins in 2023, and note that an own-history fill anchored on 2023 would inherit the defect.
rulings.rationale: The offense mix is impossible: 0/3/0/13/6/8/10 gives larceny 8 sitting BELOW agg assault 13 and below MVT 10 for a sheriff serving 17,420 people. Nationally larceny runs roughly 4-6x motor vehicle theft and 4x burglary, and far above aggravated assault; a larceny rate of 46/100k against a national ~1,300 is a missing feed, not a low-crime county. COMPOSITION OVER SLOPE is exactly the applicable test here — the smooth 146 -> 128 -> 75 -> 40 path is not evidence the 40 is genuine, and the category hole settles it independently of the slope. Full measured 12-month coverage in both lanes rules out a partial-year explanation and rules in a within-submission content failure.

rulings.detail: Property-channel truncation on a one-year cliff. Person offences look complete (15 agg assault is consistent with an agency running ~120/yr); burglary (4) and larceny (14) are at roughly a quarter of expected. EST2024=34 observed is not defensible. Do not use a month-ratio uplift — the SRS 11mo label would give only 34 x 12/11 = 37, nowhere near the deficit, which confirms this is offence-channel loss and not month truncation. Recommended basis: own-history fill from 2022-2023 (119, 112; ~116), holding the person offences as observed and reconstructing the property side.
rulings.rationale: Audrain sits on a stable three-year plateau (2021:171, 2022:119, 2023:112) and drops to 34 in one step while FBI population served is flat (11,728 -> 11,850), so no scope change is available as an explanation. The 2024 mix 0/0/0/15/4/14/1 puts agg assault (15) essentially level with larceny (14) and burglary at 4 — 118/100k larceny and 34/100k burglary for a rural sheriff jurisdiction of 11,850, several times below rural norms. The peer arm did not fire (287/100k is 46% of the 627 sheriff-band median), but the agency's own record at the same population settles it without needing peers.

rulings.detail: token_report_treat_as_partial in effect, but the failure is content-completeness, not month-coverage: mark 2024 missing and fillable. 2023 (total 5, same signature) must be marked contaminated too, so the fill basis has to skip it — use own 2021-2022 full years (54, 38) or the peer band (1096.9/100k x 5,493 = ~60); both converge on ~40-60. EST2024=7 observed is not defensible, and a month-ratio repair is not either (7 x 12/10 = 8.4).
rulings.rationale: The 2024 vector is 0/2/0/4/1/0/0 — zero larceny and zero motor vehicle theft in a 5,493-person city on the US-54/63 corridor, with rape and agg assault carrying the entire count. Larceny is never zero at that scale; this is the composition-over-slope signature of a selective feed, not a trend. 2023 shows the same collapse (5 against a 2021-2022 level of 54/38), so this is a two-year feed failure rather than an 87% crime decline. All three lanes carry the same 7, so the ladder discarded nothing larger; CIUS's 12mo is a pipeline assumption and the only measured month count (SRS 10mo) cannot rescue the value.

rulings.detail: Keep EST2024=30 observed. No repair. Optional: mark the own-history baseline as low-power (n=2 full-year rows) so the c2 arm does not re-fire on this ORI.
rulings.rationale: The peer-rate arm did NOT fire here — only c2 (own-history), and that baseline is built on just two full-year rows (2021=64, 2022=165), with 165 the clear outlier for an 8k-population rural remainder. On a per-month basis the series is 4.2/mo (2018), 6.4/mo (2020), 5.3/mo (2021), 13.8/mo (2022), 1.8/mo (2023), 2.5/mo (2024): 2024 is an INCREASE over 2023, not a collapse. The offense mix (1 rape / 12 agg assault / 3 burglary / 14 larceny) is spread across all four major categories rather than one category carrying the year, which is a thin full feed, not a partial feed; NIB and SRS independently agree at 12 months with the identical vector, so the ladder discarded nothing larger.

rulings.detail: token_report_treat_as_partial — roughly 3-4 months of content is believable (18 against an expected ~63-71). Mark 2024 missing and fill from own history: 2018-2023 median 63, 2021-2023 median 71. No month-ratio repair is available because both lanes report 12mo, so this requires a completeness override rather than an uplift. EST2024=18 observed is not defensible.
rulings.rationale: The 2024 vector 0/0/0/8/3/5/2 puts agg assault at 44% of Part-I and property at only 55%, for a sheriff that historically ran 40-91 with the normal ~85% property share. Agg-assault dominance with larceny below it is the same inverted signature as Fillmore in this batch, and it appears alongside a 4x one-year collapse from a stable 2018-2023 band. Confidence is medium rather than high because both lanes carry a full 12 months and the peer-rate arm did not fire (271/100k), so composition and own-history level are the only failing tests. Those two together are still not something a genuine decline produces.

rulings.detail: Not a credible full year. Treat as partial with roughly 3-4 months of believable coverage (66 x 4 = 264 lands on the agency's own 2021-2022 level of 268-285), or equivalently fill from own recent full years discounted for the genuine larceny trend — call it 200-270, not 66. EST2024=66 observed is not defensible. All three lanes carry the same 66, so the multi-lane hint is a non-issue; the defect is inside the single submission.
rulings.rationale: Composition, not slope, condemns it: 0/0/0/3/3/56/4 puts 85% of Part-I in larceny while burglary sits at 3, robbery and rape at 0, for a 9,556-person I-70 city whose own recent totals were 285 and 268. Burglary-3-against-larceny-56 (ratio 0.05) is the stated partial-feed signature; the contrast with Newport in this same batch (ratio 0.26, complete mix, above peer floor) is exactly the discrimination the composition test is for. The 431->323->304->285->268->151->66 run tracks the post-2020 NIBRS onboarding and decays smoothly, which I treat as no evidence either way, and 691/100k is 63% of the band peer median.

rulings.detail: Effectively a non-report — discard the SPUB 1 and mark 2024 missing. Do not uplift the fragment (1 x 12/3 = 4 is meaningless). Own-history fill is unavailable under the within-2-years rule since the last real submission was 2020. Fill from the local_police (1000, 2500] peer band but flag it hard: the peer median implies ~7 offences while Edwards' own last real years were 54, 35 and 18 (~3,500/100k), so a plain peer fill will understate badly — best marked low-confidence. Upstream: extend _drop_state_publication_non_reports to catch SPUB rows with fewer than 7 offence rows sitting on a 0-month FBI year, not only all-zero rows.
rulings.rationale: The FBI record shows zero months submitted in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 — four straight years of total non-report — and there is no NIBRS row because the roster shows nibrs_start 2024-10-01, meaning the agency only onboarded in October 2024. The sole 2024 value is a MS TOPS row with a single populated offence cell (larceny=1, NoF7 with 1 of 7 rows) that the pipeline stamped 12mo/high/weight-1.0 because SPUB carries no period field. It survived the existing non-report filter only because its total is 1 rather than 0 — the identical artifact one unit above the threshold. EST2024 = 1 publishes a one-offence year for a town whose last real measurement was 18-54.

rulings.detail: token_report_treat_as_partial — exactly 3 months are believable, per the FBI lanes' own months_reported. Correct 2024 is ~60 (15 x 12/3), which lands on the agency's own 2021-2022 full years (54, 59). EST2024=15 (observed x5 + partial-ratio x2) is indefensible and internally incoherent. Upstream fix: demote SPUB below the FBI submission lanes whenever an FBI lane carries an explicit months_reported for the same agency-year and the totals are identical — identical totals prove derivation, not independence. 2023 carries the same artifact (NIB 15/3mo + SRS 15/3mo) and needs the same treatment.
rulings.rationale: Both FBI lanes report the same 15 at 3 months; the MS TOPS row carries that identical 15 and is stamped 12mo/high/weight-1.0 only because SPUB has no period field and the pipeline defaults it. Identical totals across a 3-month FBI submission and a '12-month' state publication mean the state re-published the same three months under a full-year label — the canonical case of a 12mo label being a default, not a measurement. The SPUB row is itself incomplete (NoF7, 5 of 7 offence rows), which is why 2 offences fell through to the FBI lane and got a partial-ratio while 5 were kept observed. Annualizing the honest 3-month denominator reproduces the agency's own historical level (54, 59) almost exactly, which independently confirms the denominator.

rulings.detail: Treat 2024 as partial, roughly 3 months believable (24 against a ~90-110/yr baseline is ~25% of a year). EST2024=24 observed is not defensible. All three lanes (CIUS/NIB/SRS) carry the identical 24 at 12mo, so CIUS is merely echoing the submission and lane reselection fixes nothing. Recommended basis: own-history fill from 2022-2023 (111, 83; ~95-100), or a 12/3 uplift of the observed 24 (~96). Both land near 95.
rulings.rationale: A 16,237-population New Jersey borough with 13 larcenies and 2 burglaries for a full year is not a real crime distribution — larceny alone should run well over 100 at this size, and the all-offence rate of 147.8/100k is 11.1% of the peer median (1,327.2) for local police in the 10k-25k band. Own history confirms: 141, 137, 114, 57, 111, 83, then 24, on flat FBI population served (16,159 -> 16,237), so no scope change explains it. The agency has demonstrated feed instability before — its 2021 NIBRS conversion year dipped to 57 and then recovered to 111 in 2022 — which is the same mechanism recurring. Dual screen (own-history collapse plus peer floor) fired, and the composition check independently confirms a partial feed.

rulings.detail: Do not keep 38 as observed. This is a category-selective feed failure rather than a clean month truncation, so do not apply a month-ratio uplift and do not mix observed-violent with filled-property (that would reintroduce the per-offense lane selection the rule batch removed). Treat the whole agency-year as missing and fill from own recent history: 2023 = 95 at 12mo is inside the 2-year window, 2022 = 127, and scaling 95 by population growth (25,488 -> 26,713) gives ~100, so a fill of ~100-110 is the defensible repair. EST2024 = 38 [observed] is NOT defensible. All three lanes carry 38, so no larger submission was discarded.
rulings.rationale: This is the composition test in its purest form: agg assault 16 out of 38 total is 42% of the index (normally ~10%) while burglary sits at 2 and motor vehicle theft at 0 for a 26,713-person Ocean County township — the violent side held at or above prior years while the property side collapsed, which no real crime pattern produces. Zero MVT in a New Jersey shore township during the 2022-2024 statewide auto-theft surge is by itself disqualifying. At 142.3 per 100k the agency is at 9.2% of its peer median, the lowest in this batch, and Barnegat is an ordinary middle-class township with none of the enclave characteristics that would justify a genuine floor.

rulings.detail: Keep EST2024 = 21 as observed. SEPARATE DEFECT worth routing: the crosswalk assigns this tribal ORI to 35:municipal:place:3570500 = Santa Fe city at w=1 exclusive, while census_name reads 'pueblo of pojoaque'. Pueblo of Pojoaque is ~20 miles north of and outside Santa Fe city, so tribal counts are being smeared onto an 88k-population municipality. That footprint error is more consequential than the count question.
rulings.rationale: Both lanes report 12 months at the same value of 21, and SRS independently records 12 months, so the completeness label is not an assumption. The peer arm is structurally blind (FBIpop is 0/null, as it is for 4,133 of 18,728 2024 ORIs), so its silence is not evidence in either direction and I do not read it as such. Composition is consistent with the jurisdiction — agg assault 6 and larceny 14 fits a tribal PD whose call volume is dominated by the Buffalo Thunder casino/commercial corridor, where larceny-heavy and burglary-light is the expected profile rather than a partial-feed artifact. Only the own-history slope (76 to 44 to 21) fired, and slope alone is not disqualifying.

rulings.detail: Not a ladder error — NIB 36 and SRS 36 are the same value at the same 12-month coverage, so nothing larger was discarded. Treat 36 as a materially incomplete year, not a partial-month one: month coverage is genuinely full, so uplift by 12/months does not apply and would not fix it. EST2024=36 observed is not defensible. Repair basis: the 2021-2023 own-history baseline median of 138 for the unincorporated remainder of Comanche County, cross-checked against the sheriff peer band (10k-25k] median 627/100k x 21,029 = ~132. Flag the ORI for a submission-completeness review covering 2023 as well — the 2023 value of 82 already sits at ~60% of baseline, so the defect starts a year earlier than the screen fired.
rulings.rationale: The two-year path 171 (2022) -> 82 (2023) -> 36 (2024) at full 12-month coverage in both lanes is a 79% collapse with no territory change (FBI population served is flat at 19.2k-21.2k throughout). The rate arm did not formally fire but lands at 171/100k against a 627 sheriff-band median (27%), just above the ~25% firing threshold, so peer evidence corroborates rather than exonerates. The violent block is the tell: 0 murder / 0 rape / 0 robbery / 1 agg assault for 21k people served in Oklahoma, where ~10-50 agg assaults would be the expectation even at a quarter of national rates. Medium confidence because the offense mix is proportionally shaped rather than category-holed, which leaves a genuine (if steep) staffing-driven decline as a live alternative.

rulings.detail: Not a ladder error in the harmful direction — NIB 21 at 12mo was correctly preferred over SRS 21 at 11mo, but both are the same defective content. The property feed is dead. Treat 2024 (and 2023) as unusable; uplift does not apply since coverage is full. EST2024=21 observed is not defensible. Repair basis: the last clean own-years are 2021 (130) and 2022 (95) at full coverage in both lanes, giving ~95-110; cross-check against the sheriff band (10k-25k] median 627/100k x 15,894 = ~100, which agrees. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT: the 'own-history fill requires a real report within 2 years' rule will try to anchor on 2023 (13) or 2024 (21) — both defective. This ORI needs an explicit exclusion of 2023-2024 from its own-history basis, or a peer-rate fill instead.
rulings.rationale: The offense mix is decisive on its own: 0/0/0/18/0/2/1 means eighteen aggravated assaults with ZERO burglaries and TWO larcenies for a sheriff serving 15,894 people across rural Crook County, Oregon. No real jurisdiction has aggravated assault at nine times larceny and infinitely above burglary; the property-offence feed simply stopped while the violent feed continued. The break is datable to 2023, when the total fell from 95 to 13 at unchanged full month coverage. Full 12-month NIBRS coverage rules out a partial-year explanation, and both the own-history arm (16.6% of median) and the peer-rate arm (21.1% of peers) fired independently.

rulings.detail: Do not carry 56 as an observed full year — mark 2024 incomplete/low-confidence. A peer fill (1545.7/100k x 26,145 = ~404) would over-fabricate: Plum's only clean full year (2018, CIUS+SRS 215 = 807/100k) shows it genuinely runs at about half the peer median, so cap any fill at the agency's own historical rate (~200-215) rather than the band median. Roughly 6-8 months of property reporting is the believable coverage. EST2024=56 [observed] is not a defensible output; lane choice is not at fault (CIUS 56 = SRS 56, no larger submission was discarded).
rulings.rationale: Offense mix, not slope, decides it: burglary 17 against larceny 22 (national ratio is ~1:5) and a single motor vehicle theft in a 26,145-person Allegheny County borough during the 2024 Kia/Hyundai theft wave. Property offences are gutted while agg assault at 15 sits at a normal suburban level — that is a partial property feed, not a quiet town. The peer arm fires at 13.3% of the band median and the agency filed 0-11 months in four of the six prior years, so the 12mo label rests on a chronically unreliable filer. Both 2024 lanes carry the identical 56, so the ladder did not discard a larger, equally complete submission.

rulings.detail: Structural non-report: set 2024 to MISSING, not zero, and make it fillable. Fill from own history — annualized recent level is ~31-37 (2019: 31/10mo=37, 2020: 28/11mo=31, 2022: 13/5mo=31, 2023: 24/8mo=36), so ~33; the last real report (2023) is inside the 2-year recency rule. EST2024=0 observed is indefensible: the footprint is municipal:cousub Zelienople borough at w=1 EXCLUSIVE, so the printed zero deletes the entire borough's crime from the national panel.
rulings.rationale: This is the BLANK-AS-ZERO artifact in its cleanest form: SRS records months_reported = 0 for 2024 — the agency submitted nothing — while CIUS prints a full-year zero across all seven cells. CIUS is derived from the FBI submission, so it cannot corroborate it; publication without submission is not a measurement. The agency is is_nibrs False with no NIBRS lane at all, so there is no third source and nothing rescues the zero, and a 2-month or 0-month zero cannot be repaired by uplift. The borough PD was demonstrably live and filing in 2023 (24 offenses over 8 months), and the identical 2021 pattern (SRS 0 at 0 months) confirms this ORI's zeros are non-reports.

rulings.detail: 6 months believable — the SRS submission record for the same agency-year. EST2024 = 17 as observed-complete is NOT defensible. Minimum repair is the partial-month ratio, 17 x 12/6 = 34; but because the offense mix is also category-incomplete, a peer-benchmark fill for PA local_police in the 10k-25k band (1327.2/100k x 10,598 = ~141) is the more defensible target, with the ratio value as a floor. The CIUS 12-month label must not override an SRS month count from the same year.
rulings.rationale: This is the cleanest BLANK-AS-ZERO-family case in the batch: CIUS prints a row and the pipeline stamps months_reported=12 by assumption, while the only lane that measures months says 6 for the identical 17-count vector. A 12% -of-peers rate produced by a half-year feed with one live offense category is a coverage artifact, not a measurement.

The offense shape (larceny 10 / burglary 4 / agg assault 2) is internally coherent, so this is a uniform scale-down of everything rather than a real decline concentrated anywhere — the signature of a first-year NIBRS mapping that only passes part of the record through with a compliant 12-month header. rulings.detail: Not a ladder error — CIUS 47, NIB 47 and SRS 47 are all the SAME underlying submission (CIUS derives from the FBI submission and is never independent corroboration), so nothing larger was discarded. Flag for source review (likely 2024 RMS/vendor change) rather than accepting the value.

Every category is depressed 5-20x below national norms simultaneously (burglary 21/100k, agg assault 14/100k, larceny 256/100k), which is a uniform submission shortfall, not a crime trend. The three-lane agreement at exactly 47 is one fact, not three. Confidence is medium because the mechanism is a within-submission gap that this packet cannot directly test — the month-coverage fields are genuinely 12 and are measured, not assumed.

The peer-rate arm did not fire, but the property-side deficit is independently decisive without needing a peer comparison — 10 larcenies in a full year for a city this size is not a possible measurement regardless of what peers do.

rulings.detail: Flag, but flag the REGIME not the year: the defect spans 2020-2024, not 2024 alone. Note that the c2 arm did not fire — 2024 (41) is 78.8% of the 2021-2023 baseline (52) — so any single-year repair anchored on 2021-2023 would simply reproduce the defect. The only pre-break baseline is 2018-2019 (411, 350, SRS-only, before nibrs_start 2020-01-01), and a six-year-old anchor is itself unsafe given real national property-crime decline. rulings.rationale: The decline 411 -> 350 -> 169 -> 84 -> 52 -> 45 -> 41 breaks exactly at nibrs_start 2020-01-01, which is the classic NIBRS-transition attrition curve, and FBI population served is FLAT across the whole period (32,969 -> 32,501) — so the scope-narrowing explanation (SRS county-wide rollup replaced by a narrower NIBRS feed) is ruled out by the FBI's own population figure. Composition confirms the level is not real: 17 larcenies (52/100k) and 3 burglaries (9/100k) for 32,501 people, with agg assault (16) essentially matching larceny (17), the same inverted signature as Logan and Perryton. Confidence is medium because the smooth monotone shape means the correct repair unit and baseline are genuinely unresolved even though the level is clearly not a measurement.
